title.zh: 卷四十一 列傳第二十九: 楊播 楊敷
title.raw: 卷四十一 列傳第二十九: 楊播 楊敷 Volume 41 Biographies 29: Yangbo, Yang Fu

sentences.zh: 楊播 楊敷

translations.literal: Yang Bo, Yang Fu
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo and Yang Fu

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十九

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty-Nine
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 29

sentences.zh: 楊播子侃播弟椿椿子昱椿弟津津子遁逸謐謐弟愔燕子獻鄭頤楊敷子素孫玄感素弟約約從叔異敷叔父寬寬子文恩紀

translations.literal: Yang Bo's son Kan; Bo's younger brother Chun; Chun's son Yu; Chun's younger brother Jin; Jin's sons Dun, Yi, and Mi; Mi's younger brother Yin; Yanzi Xian; Zheng Yi; Yang Fu's son Su; Su's grandson Xuan'gan; Su's younger brother Yue; Yue's father's younger cousin Yi; Fu's father's younger brother Kuan; Kuan's sons Wen, En, and Ji
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo's son Kan; Bo's younger brother Chun; Chun's son Yu; Chun's younger brother Jin; Jin's sons Dun, Yi, and Mi; Mi's younger brother Yin; Yanzi Xian; Zheng Yi; Yang Fu's son Su; Su's grandson Xuan'gan; Su's younger brother Yue; Yue's father's younger cousin Yi; Fu's uncle Kuan; Kuan's sons Wen, En, and Ji

sentences.zh: 楊播，字延慶，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Bo, style name Yanqing, was a man of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bo, whose style name was Yanqing, came from Huayin in Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖結，仕慕容氏，位中山相。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jie served the Murong clan and held the post of Chancellor of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jie had served the Murong and risen to chancellor of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖珍，道武時歸國，位上谷太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhen returned to the state in the time of Emperor Daowu and became Administrator of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhen submitted to the Wei in the reign of Emperor Daowu and was appointed administrator of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 祖真，河內、清河二郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen served as Administrator of the two commanderies of Henei and Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had been administrator of both Henei and Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父懿，延興末為廣平太守，有稱績。

translations.literal: His father Yi, at the end of the Yanxing era, was Administrator of Guangping and won a reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi, late in the Yanxing era, served as administrator of Guangping and earned a name for solid performance.

sentences.zh: 孝文南巡，吏人頌之，徵為選部給事中，有公平譽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen toured the south, officials and people praised him; he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary in the Selection Bureau and gained a reputation for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen made his southern tour, local officials and commoners praised Yi; he was recalled to the Selection Bureau as an attendant-in-ordinary and won renown for impartiality.

sentences.zh: 除安南將軍、洛州刺史，未之任，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Luozhou, but before taking up the post he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general who pacifies the south and inspector of Luozhou, but died before he could assume the post.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加弘農公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted his former office, with the added title Duke of Hongnong, and given the posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former rank, ennobled as Duke of Hongnong, and given the posthumous name Jian (Plain).

sentences.zh: 播本字元休，孝文賜改焉。

translations.literal: Bo's original style name was Yuanxiu; Emperor Xiaowen bestowed the change to Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Bo had originally been styled Yuanxiu; Emperor Wen granted him the new style name Yanqing.

sentences.zh: 母王氏，文明太后之外姑。

translations.literal: His mother was the Wang clan, a maternal aunt by marriage of Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Wang clan, was a maternal aunt by marriage of Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 播少修飭，奉養盡禮。

translations.literal: Bo from youth cultivated propriety and fulfilled every observance in supporting his parents.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bo cultivated propriety and observed every duty in caring for his parents.

sentences.zh: 擢為中散，累遷衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and successively advanced to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant and rose in stages to vice director of the court of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 與陽平王頤等出漠北擊蠕蠕，大致克獲。

translations.literal: Together with the Prince of Yangping, Yi, and others he marched north of the desert to attack the Rouran and for the most part achieved captures.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Prince of Yangping, Yi, and others on a campaign north of the desert against the Rouran and won substantial booty.

sentences.zh: 遷武衛將軍，復征蠕蠕，至居然山而還。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Martial Guard, again campaigned against the Rouran, reached Mount Juran, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the martial guard, campaigned again against the Rouran, reached Mount Juran, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南討，假前將軍，從至鐘離。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage made the southern expedition, he was given acting rank as Forward General and followed as far as Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign, Bo was given acting rank as forward general and accompanied the host to Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 師回，詔播為圓陣禦之。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, an edict ordered Bo to form a circular battle array to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's withdrawal, an edict ordered Bo to form a circular formation and hold the enemy at bay.

sentences.zh: 相拒再宿，軍人食盡，賊圍更急。

translations.literal: They faced each other for two nights; the soldiers' provisions were exhausted and the enemy encirclement grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: They stood opposed for two nights; the troops ran out of food while the enemy ring drew tighter.

sentences.zh: 播乃領精騎三百，曆其船大呼曰：「我今欲度，能戰者出。

translations.literal: Bo then led three hundred picked horsemen, passed along their boats, and shouted loudly, "I mean to cross now—whoever can fight, come out."
translations.idiomatic: Bo then led three hundred picked horsemen along the line of enemy boats and shouted, "I am crossing now—whoever means to fight, come out!"

sentences.zh: 」遂擁而濟，賊莫敢動。

translations.literal: " He then pressed through and crossed; none of the enemy dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed through and crossed; not one of the enemy dared move against him.

sentences.zh: 賜爵華陰子。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title Viscount of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 後從駕討破崔慧景、蕭愆于鄧城，進號平東將軍。

translations.literal: Later he followed the imperial carriage in defeating Cui Huijing and Xiao Yi at Dengcheng and was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the emperor in the defeat of Cui Huijing and Xiao Yi at Dengcheng and was promoted to general who pacifies the east.

sentences.zh: 時車駕耀威城沔水，上巳設宴，帝與中軍彭城王勰賭射，左衛元遙在勰朋內，而播居帝曹。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage displayed its might at the Han River fortress; on the Shangsi festival a banquet was held. The Emperor and the Central Army Commander, the Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, wagered at archery; the Left Guard Yuan Yao was in Xie's party while Bo stood in the Emperor's.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then displaying his might at the Han River fortress. On the Shangsi festival a banquet was held; the emperor and the central army commander, the Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, wagered at archery. Yuan Yao of the left guard stood in Xie's party while Bo stood in the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 遙射侯正中，籌限已滿。

translations.literal: Yao shot and hit the target dead center; the tally of points was already full.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's arrow struck the target dead center, filling the allotted tally.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「左衛籌足，右衛不得不解。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The Left Guard's tally is complete—the Right Guard cannot but yield."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The left guard's tally is full—the right guard has no choice but to concede."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「仰恃聖恩，庶幾必爭」，於是箭正中。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Relying on Your Majesty's grace, I shall surely contend," and his arrow likewise struck the center.
translations.idiomatic: " Bo replied, "Trusting in Your Majesty's grace, I shall surely contend," and his arrow likewise struck dead center.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「雖養由之妙，何復過是。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Though Yang Youbu's skill was marvelous, how could it surpass this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Yang Youbu's skill was legendary, yet how could it surpass this?"

sentences.zh: 」遂舉卮以賜播曰：「古人酒以養病，朕今賞卿之能，可謂古今殊也。

translations.literal: " He then raised a goblet and bestowed it on Bo, saying, "The ancients took wine to nurse illness; I now reward your ability—truly past and present differ."
translations.idiomatic: " He raised a goblet and presented it to Bo, saying, "The ancients drank wine to nurse illness; I now reward your prowess—a gift past and present could scarcely match."

sentences.zh: 」除太府卿，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Director of the Imperial Treasury and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed director of the imperial treasury and advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 後為華州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he became Inspector of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 至州，借人田，為御史王基所劾，除官爵，卒於家。

translations.literal: On reaching the province he borrowed others' fields; he was impeached by the censor Wang Ji, stripped of office and rank, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After taking up his post he borrowed peasants' fields; the censor Wang Ji impeached him, he was stripped of office and rank, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子侃等停柩不葬，披訴積年。

translations.literal: His son Kan and others kept the coffin unburied and submitted appeals year after year.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kan and others refused to bury the coffin and petitioned for redress year after year.

sentences.zh: 至熙平中，乃贈鎮西將軍、雍州刺史，並復其爵，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: By the Xiping era he was posthumously granted General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yongzhou; his title was also restored, with the posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiping era he was posthumously made general who guards the west and inspector of Yongzhou; his title was restored and he was given the posthumous name Zhuang (Stalwart).

sentences.zh: 侃字士業，頗愛琴書，尤好計畫。

translations.literal: Kan, style name Shiye, was quite fond of the zither and books and especially loved stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, styled Shiye, was devoted to music and books and had a particular gift for strategy.

sentences.zh: 時播一門，貴滿朝廷，子侄早通，而侃獨不交遊，公卿罕有識者。

translations.literal: At that time Bo's entire clan filled the court with honor; sons and nephews gained early access, yet Kan alone kept no company, and few among the high ministers knew him.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's whole clan then filled the court with rank; sons and nephews won early preferment, yet Kan kept to himself and few grandees even knew his name.

sentences.zh: 親朋勸其出仕，侃曰：「苟有良田，何憂晚歲，但恨無才具耳。

translations.literal: Kin and friends urged him to take office; Kan said, "If one has good fields, why worry about one's later years? I only regret lacking talent and capacity."
translations.idiomatic: Relatives urged him to enter service; Kan replied, "With good land in hand, why fret over one's later years? I only regret lacking the talent for it."

sentences.zh: 」年三十一，襲爵華陰伯。

translations.literal: " At thirty-one he inherited the title Marquis of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: " At thirty-one he succeeded to the marquisate of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史長孫承業請為錄事參軍。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yangzhou, Zhangsun Chengye, requested him as Recording Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Chengye, inspector of Yangzhou, invited him to serve as recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 梁豫州刺史裴邃規相掩襲，密購壽春人李瓜花、袁建等令為內應。

translations.literal: Pei Sui, Inspector of Yuzhou for Liang, plotted a surprise attack and secretly bought Li Guahua, Yuan Jian, and others of Shouchun to serve as inside agents.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui, Liang's inspector of Yuzhou, plotted a surprise assault and secretly enlisted Li Guahua, Yuan Jian, and other men of Shouchun as inside agents.

sentences.zh: 邃已纂勒兵士，慮壽春疑覺，遂謬移云：「魏始於馬頭置戍，如聞復欲修白捺舊城。

translations.literal: Sui had already mustered troops but feared Shouchun would grow suspicious; he therefore sent a false dispatch saying, "Wei has newly garrisoned Matou, and we hear they again mean to repair the old city of Bainuo."
translations.idiomatic: Sui had already mustered his troops but feared Shouchun would scent the plot; he therefore sent a deceptive dispatch claiming, "Wei has newly garrisoned Matou, and we hear they mean to repair the old fortress at Bainuo."

sentences.zh: 若爾，便稍相侵逼。

translations.literal: If so, they will gradually encroach upon us.
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, they will gradually press upon our borders.

sentences.zh: 此亦須營歐陽，設交境之備。

translations.literal: We too must fortify Ouyang and set defenses along the border.
translations.idiomatic: We too must fortify Ouyang and prepare defenses along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 今板卒已集，唯聽信還。

translations.literal: The carpenters and soldiers are already assembled; we await only your reply to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Labor and troops are already assembled; we await only your word to stand down.

sentences.zh: 」佐寮咸欲以實答之，雲無修白捺意。

translations.literal: " The staff all wished to answer truthfully, saying there was no intent to repair Bainuo.
translations.idiomatic: " The staff all wished to answer truthfully that Wei had no plan to repair Bainuo.

sentences.zh: 而侃曰：「白捺小城，本非形勝，邃集兵遣移，虛構是言，得無有別圖也？

translations.literal: But Kan said, "Bainuo is a small town and no strategic strongpoint; Sui has mustered troops and sent this dispatch—fabricating such talk—can he have no other design?"
translations.idiomatic: Kan objected: "Bainuo is a minor post and no strategic prize. Sui has mustered troops and invented this pretext—can he have no deeper design?"

sentences.zh: 」承業乃云：「錄事可造移報。

translations.literal: " Chengye then said, "The Recording Secretary may draft the reply dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: " Chengye said, "Let the recording secretary draft our reply."

sentences.zh: 」移曰：「彼之纂兵，想別有意，何為妄構白捺？

translations.literal: " The dispatch read, "Your mustering of troops surely has another purpose—why invent Bainuo without cause?"
translations.idiomatic: " The dispatch ran: "Your mustering of troops surely serves another purpose—why invent a tale about Bainuo?"

sentences.zh: 他人有心，予忖度之，勿謂秦無人也。

translations.literal: Others have their thoughts—I have measured them; do not suppose Qin has no men.
translations.idiomatic: Others have their designs, and I have taken their measure; do not suppose that Qin has no wise men left.

sentences.zh: 」邃得移，謂已覺，便散兵。

translations.literal: " Sui received the dispatch, judged that he had been detected, and dispersed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Sui received the dispatch, concluded he had been found out, and disbanded his army.

sentences.zh: 瓜花等以期契不會，便相告發，伏辜者十數家。

translations.literal: Guahua and others, because the appointed time failed to come together, informed on one another; more than ten households suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Guahua and the others, their rendezvous having failed, turned informer on one another; more than ten households paid with their lives.

sentences.zh: 邃後竟襲襲壽春，入羅城而退，遂列營于黎漿、梁城，日夕鈔掠。

translations.literal: Sui later still attacked Shouchun, entered the outer wall and withdrew, then pitched camps at Lijiang and Liangcheng and raided day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Sui later attacked Shouchun after all, breached the outer wall and withdrew, then encamped at Lijiang and Liangcheng and raided without cease.

sentences.zh: 承業乃奏侃為統軍。

translations.literal: Chengye then memorialized to appoint Kan as Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye memorialized to appoint Kan commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 後雍州刺史蕭寶夤據州反，隨業討之，除侃為承業行台左丞。

translations.literal: Later the Inspector of Yongzhou, Xiao Baoyin, seized the province in rebellion; Kan followed Chengye to suppress him and was appointed Left Assistant of Chengye's field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin, inspector of Yongzhou, rebelled and held the province, Kan joined Chengye's punitive campaign and was made left assistant on Chengye's field staff.

sentences.zh: 軍次恆農，侃白承業曰：「今賊守潼關，全據形勝。

translations.literal: The army halted at Hengnong; Kan told Chengye, "The rebels now hold Tong Pass and fully occupy the strategic advantage."
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Hengnong; Kan told Chengye, "The rebels hold Tong Pass and command every advantage of terrain."

sentences.zh: 須北取蒲阪，飛棹西岸，置兵死地，人有鬥心，華州之圍，可不戰而解；

translations.literal: We must strike north for Puban, send swift boats to the western bank, place troops where death is certain so that men will fight with desperate resolve—the siege of Huazhou can be lifted without battle;
translations.idiomatic: We must take Puban to the north, send swift boats to the western bank, and plant troops where retreat is impossible so they fight with desperate resolve—the siege of Huazhou can then be lifted without a battle;

sentences.zh: 潼關之賊，必望風潰散。

translations.literal: the rebels at Tong Pass will surely scatter at the mere rumor of our approach.
translations.idiomatic: the rebels at Tong Pass will scatter at the mere rumor of our approach.

sentences.zh: 諸處既平，長安自克。

translations.literal: Once the various places are pacified, Chang'an will fall of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Once the outlying posts are pacified, Chang'an will fall of itself.

sentences.zh: 愚計可錄，請為明公前驅。

translations.literal: This humble plan is worth adopting; I beg to serve Your Excellency as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: This plan is sound; allow me to serve as your vanguard.

sentences.zh: 」承業從之，令其子子產等領騎與侃于恆農北度，便據石錐壁。

translations.literal: " Chengye agreed and ordered his son Zichan and others to lead cavalry with Kan to cross north of Hengnong and immediately seize the Stone Cone cliff.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengye agreed and sent his son Zichan and others with cavalry to cross north of Hengnong with Kan; they at once seized the Stone Cone cliff.

sentences.zh: 乃班告曰：「今且停軍於此，以待步卒，兼觀人情向背。

translations.literal: They then issued a proclamation saying, "We shall halt the army here for the moment to await the infantry and also observe which way popular sentiment turns."
translations.idiomatic: They then proclaimed, "We halt here for the moment to await the infantry and to see which way the people lean."

sentences.zh: 若送降名者，各自還村，侯台軍舉三烽火，各亦應之，以明降款。

translations.literal: Those who submit names of surrender should each return to their villages; when the imperial army raises three beacon fires, each should respond likewise to show submission.
translations.idiomatic: Those who mean to surrender should return to their villages; when the imperial army raises three beacon fires, each village should answer in kind to signal submission.

sentences.zh: 其無應烽，即是不降之村，理須殄戮。

translations.literal: Any that fail to answer the beacons are villages that have not submitted and should in principle be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Any village that fails to answer is a village that has not submitted and must be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 」人遂傳相告報。

translations.literal: " The people then passed the word from one to another.
translations.idiomatic: " Word spread from village to village.

sentences.zh: 實未降者，亦詐舉烽，一宿之間，火光遍數百里內。

translations.literal: Even those who had not truly submitted falsely raised beacons; within a single night fires blazed across several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Even villages that had not truly submitted lit false beacons; within a single night fires blazed across hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 圍城之寇，不測所以，各自散歸。

translations.literal: The besieging rebels, unable to fathom what was happening, each scattered homeward.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers, unable to fathom what was happening, broke up and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 長安平，侃頗有力焉。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, Kan had contributed substantially.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an fell, Kan had contributed substantially to the victory.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除岐州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was appointed Inspector of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era he was appointed inspector of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 屬元顥內逼，詔行北中郎將。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, an edict made him acting Northern Central Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed inward on the capital, an edict appointed him acting northern central commander.

sentences.zh: 孝莊徙河北，執侃手曰：「朕停卿蕃寄，移任此者，正為今日。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang moved to Hebei, took Kan's hand, and said, "I kept you in a frontier post and transferred you here precisely for this day."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang withdrew to Hebei, took Kan's hand, and said, "I kept you in a frontier post and moved you here precisely for this day."

sentences.zh: 但卿尊卑百口，若隨朕行，所累處大。

translations.literal: But your household, high and low, numbers a hundred mouths; if you follow me on the march, the burden would be great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your household, high and low together, numbers a hundred mouths; if you march with me, the burden on the army would be heavy.

sentences.zh: 卿可還洛，寄之後圖。

translations.literal: You may return to Luoyang and entrust yourself to plans for later.
translations.idiomatic: Return to Luoyang and trust to what may come afterward.

sentences.zh: 」侃曰：「寧可以臣微族，頓廢君臣之義。

translations.literal: " Kan said, "How could this humble clan of mine abruptly abandon the duty between ruler and subject?"
translations.idiomatic: " Kan replied, "How could my humble clan abruptly cast aside the bond between ruler and subject?"

sentences.zh: 」固求陪從。

translations.literal: " He firmly begged to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: " He insisted on accompanying the emperor.

sentences.zh: 除度支尚書，兼給事黃門侍郎，敷西縣公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Revenue, concurrently Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fuxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of revenue and concurrent attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fuxi county.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南還，顥令梁將陳慶之守北中城，自據南岸。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned south, Hao ordered the Liang general Chen Qingzhi to hold the North Central fortress while he himself occupied the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned south, Hao ordered the Liang general Chen Qingzhi to hold the north-central fortress while he himself took the south bank.

sentences.zh: 有夏州義士為顥守河中渚，乃密信通款，求破橋立效。

translations.literal: A loyalist of Xiazhou was holding the mid-river islet for Hao; he sent a secret letter offering allegiance and asked to destroy the bridge to prove his merit.
translations.idiomatic: A loyalist of Xiazhou holding a mid-river islet for Hao sent a secret letter offering allegiance and proposing to break the bridge as proof of his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮赴之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong hastened to the scene.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong hurried to the crossing.

sentences.zh: 及橋破，應接不果，皆為顥屠。

translations.literal: When the bridge was broken, the planned rendezvous failed and all were slaughtered by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When the bridge was broken the planned link-up failed, and Hao's men slaughtered them all.

sentences.zh: 榮將為還計，欲更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Rong was about to plan a withdrawal and seek another opportunity later.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was readying a withdrawal and meant to wait for a better moment.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「若今即還，人情失望，未若召發人材，唯多縛筏，間以舟楫，沿河廣布。

translations.literal: Kan said, "If we withdraw now, men's hearts will lose hope. Better to summon labor and materials, bind many rafts, intersperse boats, and spread them widely along the river."
translations.idiomatic: Kan urged, "If we withdraw now, men's hearts will fail. Better to summon labor and timber, bind rafts in great numbers, mix in boats, and spread the fleet widely along the river."

sentences.zh: 令數百里中，皆為度勢，顥知防何處？

translations.literal: Let the crossing posture extend for several hundred li—how will Hao know where to defend?
translations.idiomatic: Let the appearance of a crossing stretch for hundreds of li—how will Hao know where to defend?

sentences.zh: 一旦得度，必立大功。

translations.literal: Once we cross in a single stroke, we are sure to win great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once we cross somewhere, we are sure to win a great victory.

sentences.zh: 」榮大笑從之。

translations.literal: " Rong laughed loudly and followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong laughed and took his advice.

sentences.zh: 於是爾硃兆等於馬渚諸楊南度，顥便南走。

translations.literal: Thereupon Erzhu Zhao and others crossed south of the Zhuyang ford at Mazhu, and Hao at once fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao and others then crossed south of the Zhuyang ford at Mazhu, and Hao fled south at once.

sentences.zh: 車駕入都，侃解尚書，正黃門。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered the capital, Kan was relieved of the ministry post and made regular Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the capital, Kan was relieved of the ministry and confirmed as attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 以濟河功，進爵濟北郡公，復除其長子師仲為秘書郎。

translations.literal: For the merit of crossing the river he was advanced to Duke of Jibei commandery, and his eldest son Shizhong was again appointed Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in the river crossing he was advanced to Duke of Jibei commandery, and his eldest son Shizhong was again appointed secretary.

sentences.zh: 時所用錢，人多私鑄，稍就薄小，乃至風飄水浮，米斗幾直一千。

translations.literal: The coin then in use was largely privately cast, gradually growing thin and small, until it would drift in wind and float on water; a dou of grain cost nearly a thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The currency then in circulation was largely privately cast, growing ever thinner and lighter until coins would drift in the wind and float on water; a dou of grain cost nearly a thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 侃奏聽人與官並鑄五銖，使人樂為，而俗弊得改。

translations.literal: Kan memorialized to allow private persons and the government alike to cast wuzhu coins, so that men would gladly do so and the corrupt custom could be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Kan memorialized to permit private persons and the government alike to cast wuzhu coins, so that people would willingly mint sound money and the debased custom might be corrected.

sentences.zh: 莊帝從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 後除侍中，加衛將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Palace Attendant, with the added titles General of the Guard and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made palace attendant, with the added titles general of the guard and right grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 莊帝將圖爾硃榮，侃與內弟李晞、城陽王徽、侍中李彧等咸預其謀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was plotting against Erzhu Rong, Kan together with his brother-in-law Li Xi, the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, the Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Yu, and others all took part in the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang plotted against Erzhu Rong, Kan joined his brother-in-law Li Xi, the Prince of Chengyang, Hui, the attendant-in-ordinary Li Yu, and others in the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 爾硃兆入洛，侃時休沐，遂竄歸華陰。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Kan was on leave and fled back to Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Kan was on leave and fled home to Huayin.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，天光在關西，遣侃子婦父韋義遠招慰之，立盟許恕其罪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, Tian Guang was in the western passes and sent Kan's father-in-law Wei Yiyuan to summon and reassure him, establishing a covenant that promised forgiveness of his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putai era, Tian Guang held the western passes and sent Kan's father-in-law Wei Yiyuan to summon and reassure him, swearing a covenant that promised pardon.

sentences.zh: 侃從兄昱恐為家禍，令侃出應，假其食言，不過一人身沒，冀全百口。

translations.literal: Kan's older cousin Yu feared disaster for the clan and urged Kan to go out and answer the summons, wagering that even if they broke their word, at most one man would perish and a hundred mouths might be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's cousin Yu feared ruin for the whole clan and urged him to answer the summons, wagering that even if Tian Guang broke his oath, at most one man would die while a hundred kinsmen might be spared.

sentences.zh: 侃赴之，為天光所害。

translations.literal: Kan went and was killed by Tian Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Kan went—and Tian Guang killed him.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈車騎將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously granted General of the Cavalry and Chariots, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era he was posthumously made general of the cavalry and chariots, with honors equal to the three excellencies, and inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 子純陀襲。

translations.literal: His son Chuntuo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuntuo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 播弟椿。

translations.literal: Bo's younger brother Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's younger brother was Chun.

sentences.zh: 椿字延壽，本字仲考，孝文賜改焉。

translations.literal: Chun, style name Yanshou, had originally been styled Zhongkao; Emperor Xiaowen bestowed the change.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, styled Yanshou, had originally been named Zhongkao; Emperor Wen granted him the new style name.

sentences.zh: 性寬謹。

translations.literal: His nature was generous and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature generous and cautious.

sentences.zh: 為內給事，與兄播並侍禁闈。

translations.literal: He served as Inner Attendant and together with his elder brother Bo attended within the forbidden quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served as inner attendant and, together with his elder brother Bo, attended within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 後為中部法曹，折訟公正，孝文嘉之。

translations.literal: Later he was in the Central Legal Bureau, deciding lawsuits with fairness; Emperor Xiaowen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in the central legal bureau, judging cases with impartiality; Emperor Wen commended him.

sentences.zh: 及文明太后崩，孝文五日不食。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, Emperor Xiaowen went five days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, Emperor Wen fasted for five days.

sentences.zh: 椿諫曰：「聖人之禮，毀不滅性，從陛下欲自賢於萬代，其若宗廟何！

translations.literal: Chun remonstrated, saying, "In the rites of the sages, mourning does not destroy one's nature. If Your Majesty wishes to make yourself more virtuous than all ages, what of the ancestral temple!"
translations.idiomatic: Chun remonstrated: "The sages taught that mourning must not destroy one's vital nature. If Your Majesty wishes to outshine every age in virtue, what becomes of the ancestral temple?"

sentences.zh: 」帝感其言，乃一進粥。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was moved by his words and then took one bowl of gruel.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was moved and took a single bowl of gruel.

sentences.zh: 轉授宮輿曹少卿，加給事中，出為豫州刺史，再遷梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Carriages Bureau, added as Attendant-in-Ordinary, sent out as Inspector of Yuzhou, and again transferred to Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the imperial carriages bureau and attendant-in-ordinary, then sent out as inspector of Yuzhou and later transferred to inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，武興王楊集始降于齊，自漢中而北，規復舊土。

translations.literal: Earlier the Prince of Wuxing, Yang Jishi, had submitted to Qi; from Hanzhong he marched north, plotting to recover his former lands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Wuxing, Yang Jishi, had defected to Qi and marched north from Hanzhong, intending to recover his former territory.

sentences.zh: 椿貽書集始，開以利害。

translations.literal: Chun sent Jishi a letter setting forth advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Chun wrote to Jishi, laying out the costs and benefits of his course.

sentences.zh: 集始執書對使者曰：「楊使君此書，除我心腹疾。

translations.literal: Jishi took the letter and said to the envoy, "Commissioner Yang's letter has cured the ailment in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Jishi took the letter and told the envoy, "Commissioner Yang's letter has lifted the sickness from my heart."

sentences.zh: 」遂來降。

translations.literal: " He then came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老解還。

translations.literal: Soon, because his mother was aged, he was relieved and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on account of his aged mother, he was relieved and returned home.

sentences.zh: 後兼太僕卿。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made concurrent director of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 秦州羌呂苟兒、涇州屠各陳瞻等反，詔椿為別將，隸安西將軍元麗討之。

translations.literal: The Qiang Lü Gou'er of Qinzhou and the Tuge Chen Zhan of Jingzhou and others rebelled; an edict appointed Chun as Separate Commander under the General Who Pacifies the West, Yuan Li, to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang Lü Gou'er of Qinzhou and the Tuge Chen Zhan of Jingzhou rebelled, an edict made Chun a separate commander under the general who pacifies the west, Yuan Li.

sentences.zh: 賊守峽自固。

translations.literal: The rebels held the pass and fortified themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the gorge and dug in.

sentences.zh: 或謀伏兵斷其出入，待糧盡攻之。

translations.literal: Some proposed ambushing troops to cut off their entry and exit and attacking when their provisions were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged ambushing the passes and waiting until their grain ran out before attacking.

sentences.zh: 或云斬山木，從火焚之。

translations.literal: Others said to cut the mountain timber and set fire to burn them out.
translations.idiomatic: Others proposed felling the timber on the slopes and burning them out with fire.

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「並非計也。

translations.literal: Chun said, "Neither is a sound plan."
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "Neither plan will do."

sentences.zh: 賊深竄，正避死耳。

translations.literal: The rebels have burrowed deep—they are simply avoiding death.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels have burrowed deep; they are simply trying to stay alive.

sentences.zh: 今宜勒三軍勿更侵掠，賊必謂見險不前，心輕我軍，然後掩其不備，可一舉而平。

translations.literal: Now we should order the three armies to cease further raiding; the rebels will surely think that seeing the danger we dare not advance, and will despise our army in their hearts—then we can strike when they are unprepared and pacify them in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: We should order the armies to cease raiding; the rebels will think we shrink from the terrain and grow contemptuous—then we can strike when they are unprepared and end the rebellion in a single blow.

sentences.zh: 」乃緩師。

translations.literal: " They then slowed the advance.
translations.idiomatic: " The army slowed its advance.

sentences.zh: 賊果出掠，仍以軍中驢馬餌之。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed came out to raid, and they again used the army's donkeys and horses as bait.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels duly came out to raid, and the army again used its donkeys and horses as bait.

sentences.zh: 銜枚夜襲，斬瞻傳首。

translations.literal: With gags in their mouths they raided by night, beheaded Zhan, and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked by night with gags in their mouths, beheaded Zhan, and sent his head to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 入正太僕卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as regular Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as full director of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 初，獻文世有蠕蠕萬餘戶降附，居於高平、薄骨律二鎮。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the reign of Emperor Xianwen, more than ten thousand Rouran households had submitted and were settled in the two garrisons of Gaoping and Bogulu.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Xianwen, more than ten thousand Rouran households had submitted and been settled at the garrisons of Gaoping and Bogulu.

sentences.zh: 太和末叛走，唯有一千餘家。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe era most rebelled and fled; only a little more than a thousand households remained.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taihe era most rebelled and fled, leaving only a little more than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 太中大夫王通、高平鎮將郎育等求徙置淮北，防其後叛。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Palace Counsel Wang Tong, the Gaoping garrison commander Lang Yu, and others requested that they be moved and settled north of the Huai to guard against later rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong, grand master of palace counsel, Lang Yu, commander of the Gaoping garrison, and others asked that the remnant be moved north of the Huai to forestall another rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔椿徙焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chun to carry out the relocation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chun to carry out the move.

sentences.zh: 椿上書，以為裔不謀夏，夷不亂華，是以先朝居之荒服之間，正欲悅近來遠。

translations.literal: Chun submitted a memorial, holding that distant peoples do not plot against the central states and barbarians do not disturb the civilized realm; therefore the former court settled them in the borderlands precisely to delight those near and draw those far.
translations.idiomatic: Chun memorialized that distant peoples do not plot against the central states and barbarians do not disturb the civilized realm; the former court had settled them on the frontier precisely to win those near and draw those far.

sentences.zh: 今新附者眾，若舊者見徙，新者必不安，愚謂不可。

translations.literal: Now many have newly submitted; if the old settlers are seen to be moved, the new ones will surely grow uneasy—I humbly hold this inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: Many have newly submitted; if the old settlers are moved, the newcomers will surely grow uneasy. I hold that the move is inadvisable.

sentences.zh: 時八坐不從，遂於濟州緣河居之。

translations.literal: The Eight Ministers did not follow his advice, and the people were therefore settled along the river in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The eight ministers overruled him, and the settlers were placed along the river in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 及冀州元愉之難，果悉浮河赴賊，所在鈔掠，如椿所策。

translations.literal: When the trouble of Yuan Yu in Jizhou arose, they indeed all crossed the river by raft to join the rebels and raided wherever they went, just as Chun had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yu rebelled in Jizhou, they all crossed the river by raft to join him and raided wherever they went, exactly as Chun had predicted.

sentences.zh: 後除朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made inspector of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 在州為廷尉奏椿前為太僕卿，招引百姓，盜種牧田三百四十頃，依律處刑五歲。

translations.literal: While in the province the Minister of Justice memorialized that when Chun had earlier been Director of the Imperial Stud he had enticed commoners to illicitly cultivate three hundred forty qing of pasture land; by law he should be punished with five years' penal service.
translations.idiomatic: While he held the province, the minister of justice reported that as director of the imperial stud Chun had induced commoners to illicitly farm three hundred forty qing of pasture; by law he merited five years' penal service.

sentences.zh: 尚書邢巒據正始別格，奏罪應除名，注籍盜門，同籍合門不仕。

translations.literal: The Minister Xing Luan, citing the separate statutes of the Zhengshi era, memorialized that the crime warranted removal from the register, entry in the register of thieves, and that those of the same register and combined households should not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xing Luan, citing the separate statutes of the Zhengshi era, argued that the offense warranted removal from office, registration in the thieves' roll, and disqualification of the entire household from service.

sentences.zh: 宣武以親律既班，不宜雜用舊制，詔依斷，以贖論。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu held that since the statutes for kin had been promulgated, the old system should not be mixed in; an edict followed the judgment but allowed redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu held that with the new kin statutes in force the old penalties should not apply; an edict confirmed the judgment but allowed redemption.

sentences.zh: 後除定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 自道武平中山，多置軍府，以相威攝。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, many military offices were established to exert mutual deterrence.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, numerous military offices had been established to keep one another in check.

sentences.zh: 凡有八軍，軍各配兵五千，食祿主帥軍各四十六人。

translations.literal: There were eight armies in all; each army was allotted five thousand troops, and each army had forty-six salaried commanders.
translations.idiomatic: There were eight armies in all, each with five thousand troops and forty-six salaried commanders.

sentences.zh: 自中原稍定，八軍之兵漸割南戍，一軍兵才千餘，然主帥如故，費祿不少。

translations.literal: Once the central plains were gradually pacified, the troops of the eight armies were progressively assigned to southern garrisons; each army had barely a thousand men, yet the commanders remained as before and salary expenses were not small.
translations.idiomatic: As the central plains grew settled, the eight armies were gradually stripped to garrison the south; each army mustered barely a thousand men, yet the full complement of commanders remained and salaries still ran high.

sentences.zh: 椿表罷四軍，減其主帥百八十四人。

translations.literal: Chun memorialized to abolish four armies and reduce their commanders by one hundred eighty-four men.
translations.idiomatic: Chun memorialized to abolish four armies and cut one hundred eighty-four commanders.

sentences.zh: 椿在州，因修黑山道餘功，伐木私造佛寺，役兵，為御史所劾，除名。

translations.literal: While Chun was in the province, using surplus labor from repairing the Heishan road, he felled timber to build a Buddhist temple on his own authority and impressed soldiers; he was impeached by the censor and stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: While in the province Chun used surplus labor from the Heishan road project to fell timber and build a private Buddhist temple, impressing troops in the process; a censor impeached him and he was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 後累遷為雍州刺史，進號車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Yongzhou and advanced to General of the Cavalry and Chariots, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to inspector of Yongzhou and was advanced to general of the cavalry and chariots with honors equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官加侍中，兼尚書右僕射，為行台，節度關西諸將。

translations.literal: Soon on his existing office he was added as Palace Attendant and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, made field headquarters, and placed in command of the generals west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made palace attendant and concurrent right vice director of the imperial secretariat, appointed to a field headquarters, and given command of the generals west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 遇暴疾，頻啟乞解，詔許之，以蕭寶夤代為刺史、行台。

translations.literal: He suffered a sudden illness and repeatedly memorialized begging to be relieved; an edict granted it, and Xiao Baoyin was appointed in his place as inspector and field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken with a sudden illness, he repeatedly begged to be relieved; the throne agreed and appointed Xiao Baoyin in his place as inspector and field commander.

sentences.zh: 椿還鄉里，遇子昱將還京師，使陳寶夤賞罰雲為，不依常憲，恐有異心。

translations.literal: Chun returned to his home district and met his son Yu, who was about to return to the capital; he had Yu report that Xiao Baoyin's rewards and punishments were arbitrary and did not follow regular statutes, and that he feared treacherous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chun returned home and met his son Yu, who was bound for the capital; he had Yu report that Xiao Baoyin's rewards and punishments were arbitrary and outside the statutes, and that he suspected disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 昱還，面啟明帝及靈太后，並不納。

translations.literal: Yu returned and reported in person to Emperor Ming and Empress Dowager Ling; neither accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reported in person to Emperor Ming and Empress Dowager Ling; neither would heed the warning.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤邀害禦只中尉酈道元，猶上表自理，稱為椿父子所謗。

translations.literal: When Baoyin lured and killed the Attendant of the Imperial Clan, Li Daoyuan, he still submitted a memorial in his own defense, claiming he had been slandered by Chun and his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin ambushed and killed the attendant of the imperial clan Li Daoyuan, he still memorialized in self-defense, claiming he had been slandered by Chun and his sons.

sentences.zh: 建義元年，為司徒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyi he was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyi he was appointed minister of education.

sentences.zh: 永安初，進位太保，加侍中，給後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was advanced to Grand Tutor, added as Palace Attendant, and granted rear guard music.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yong'an era he was advanced to grand tutor, made palace attendant, and granted imperial music for his rear guard.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，椿子昱為顥禽。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Chun's son Yu was captured by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Chun's son Yu was taken by Hao.

sentences.zh: 又椿弟順、順子仲宣、兄子侃、弟子遁並從駕河內，為顥嫌疑。

translations.literal: Moreover Chun's younger brother Shun, Shun's son Zhongxuan, his elder brother's son Kan, and his younger brother's son Dun all followed the imperial carriage at Henei and were suspected by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Shun, Shun's son Zhongxuan, his nephew Kan, and his younger brother's son Dun had all accompanied the emperor to Henei and fell under Hao's suspicion.

sentences.zh: 以椿家世顯重，恐失人望，未及加罪。

translations.literal: Because Chun's clan was illustrious and weighty, Hao feared losing popular regard and did not reach the point of punishing them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Yang clan was too eminent to offend lightly, Hao feared losing popular support and did not punish them.

sentences.zh: 時人助其憂，或勸椿攜家避禍。

translations.literal: People of the time shared his anxiety; some urged Chun to take his household and flee disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Others shared his anxiety and urged Chun to flee with his household.

sentences.zh: 椿曰：「吾內外百口，何處逃竄？

translations.literal: Chun said, "Within and without, we are a hundred mouths—where could we flee?"
translations.idiomatic: Chun said, "Within and without, we number a hundred mouths—where could we flee?"

sentences.zh: 正當坐任運耳。」

translations.literal: We can only sit and trust to fate."
translations.idiomatic: We can only sit and leave it to fate."

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，椿上書頻請歸老，詔聽服侍中服，賜朝服一襲、八尺床帳、幾、杖，不朝，乘安車，駕駟馬，給扶，傳詔二人，仰所在郡縣四時以禮存問安否。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Chun repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; an edict permitted him to wear the attire of a Palace Attendant, granted one set of court robes, an eight-foot bed canopy, a table, and a staff, exempted him from court attendance, allowed him to ride in a comfort carriage drawn by four horses with attendants to support him, and assigned two edict-bearers, charging the commandery and county of his residence to inquire after his health by ritual observance in the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, Chun repeatedly begged to retire. An edict permitted him to wear attendant's robes, granted court dress, an eight-foot bed canopy, a table, and a staff, exempted him from court, allowed a comfort carriage drawn by four horses with bearers to assist him, and assigned two edict-bearers, charging his home commandery and county to inquire after his health each season.

sentences.zh: 椿奉辭于華林園，帝下御座，執手流淚曰：「公先帝舊臣，實為元老。

translations.literal: Chun took leave at the Hualin Garden; the Emperor descended from the throne, took his hand with tears, and said, "You are an old minister of the former emperor—truly a senior statesman."
translations.idiomatic: Chun took leave at the Hualin Garden. The emperor descended from the throne, took his hand in tears, and said, "You are an old minister of my predecessor—truly the elder statesman of the court."

sentences.zh: 但高尚其志，決意不留，既難相違，深用淒切。

translations.literal: Yet you elevate your will and are resolved not to remain; since it is hard to go against you, I am deeply grieved."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you hold your principles high and are resolved to go; since I cannot keep you, my grief is profound."

sentences.zh: 」椿亦歔欷，欲拜，帝親執不聽。

translations.literal: " Chun too sobbed; wishing to bow, the Emperor personally held him and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: " Chun sobbed as well and moved to bow, but the emperor held him and would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 賜以絹布，給羽林衛送。

translations.literal: He was granted silk and cloth, and the Feathered Forest guard was assigned to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted silk and cloth, and the Feathered Forest guard escorted him home.

sentences.zh: 群公百寮餞于城西張方橋，行路觀者莫不稱歎。

translations.literal: The assembled lords and hundred officials gave him a farewell at Zhangfang Bridge west of the city; passersby who watched all praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled lords and officials gave him a farewell at Zhangfang Bridge west of the city; every passerby who watched sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 椿臨行，誡子孫曰：

translations.literal: As Chun was about to depart, he admonished his sons and grandsons, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, Chun admonished his sons and grandsons:

sentences.zh: 我家入魏之始，即為上客。

translations.literal: From the time our house entered Wei we have been honored guests.
translations.idiomatic: From the day our house entered Wei we have been honored guests of the throne.

sentences.zh: 自爾至今，二千石方伯不絕，祿恤甚多。

translations.literal: From then until now, two-thousand-bushel regional lords have never ceased, and salaries and stipends have been abundant.
translations.idiomatic: From then until now, governors of two-thousand-bushel rank have never ceased in our line, and salaries and stipends have been abundant.

sentences.zh: 於親姻知故吉凶之際，必厚加贈襚；

translations.literal: At the moments of fortune and misfortune among kin, in-laws, and old friends, we have always given lavish funeral gifts;
translations.idiomatic: At weddings and funerals among kin, in-laws, and old friends we have always given lavish gifts;

sentences.zh: 來往賓寮，必以酒肉飲食，故六姻朋友無憾焉。

translations.literal: guests who come and go have always been treated with wine and meat, so that the six degrees of kinship and friends have had no cause for regret.
translations.idiomatic: guests who come and go have always been feasted with wine and meat, so that kin and friends have had no cause for complaint.

sentences.zh: 國家初，丈夫好服彩色。

translations.literal: When the state was first founded, men liked to wear bright colors.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding days of the state, men liked to dress in bright colors.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不記上谷翁時事，然記清河翁時服飾。

translations.literal: I do not remember affairs in the time of the Shanggu elder, but I remember the dress of the Qinghe elder's day.
translations.idiomatic: I do not recall affairs in the time of the Shanggu elder, but I remember how the Qinghe elder dressed.

sentences.zh: 恆見翁著布衣韋帶，常自約敕諸父曰：「汝等後世若富貴於今日者，慎勿積金一斤、彩帛百匹已上，用為富也。

translations.literal: I constantly saw the elder wearing plain cloth and a leather belt; he often admonished his brothers, saying, "If you later become richer than today, take care not to amass more than one jin of gold or a hundred bolts of colored silk as your wealth."
translations.idiomatic: I always saw him in plain cloth and a leather belt. He often admonished his brothers: "If you later grow richer than we are today, take care not to amass more than one jin of gold or a hundred bolts of colored silk."

sentences.zh: 」不聽興生求利，又不聽與勢家作婚姻。

translations.literal: " He would not permit engaging in trade for profit, nor would he permit marriage alliances with powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: " He forbade trade for profit and forbade marriage alliances with powerful families.

sentences.zh: 至吾兄弟，不能遵奉。

translations.literal: As for us brothers, we could not follow and uphold this.
translations.idiomatic: We brothers could not live up to his example.

sentences.zh: 今汝等服乘漸華好，吾是以知恭儉之德，漸不如上也。

translations.literal: Now your dress and mounts grow ever more splendid; I therefore know that the virtue of respect and frugality is gradually falling short of the generation above.
translations.idiomatic: Your dress and mounts grow ever more splendid; I see that respect and frugality are fading with each generation.

sentences.zh: 又吾兄弟，若在家，必同盤而食；

translations.literal: Moreover, when we brothers were at home we always ate from the same dish;
translations.idiomatic: When we brothers were at home we always ate from the same dish;

sentences.zh: 若有近行，不至，必待其還。

translations.literal: if one made a short trip and had not returned, we would certainly wait for him to come back.
translations.idiomatic: if one was away on a short errand, we waited until he returned.

sentences.zh: 亦有過中不食，忍饑相待。

translations.literal: There were times when we passed midday without eating, enduring hunger while we waited for one another.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes we passed midday without eating, enduring hunger while we waited.

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟八人，今存者有三，是故不忍別食也。

translations.literal: We were eight brothers; only three survive today—therefore we could not bear to eat apart.
translations.idiomatic: We were eight brothers; only three survive today—that is why we could not bear to eat apart.

sentences.zh: 又願畢吾兄弟，不異居異財。

translations.literal: I also wish that for the rest of our brothers' lives you will not live separately or hold separate property.
translations.idiomatic: I also charge you: for the rest of our days, do not live apart or hold separate estates.

sentences.zh: 汝等眼見，非為虛假。

translations.literal: You have seen this with your own eyes—it is no empty pretense.
translations.idiomatic: You have seen this yourselves—it is no empty lesson.

sentences.zh: 如聞汝等兄弟，時有別齋獨食者。

translations.literal: I hear that among you brothers there are some who sometimes take separate rooms and eat alone.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that some of you brothers now take separate rooms and eat alone.

sentences.zh: 此又不如吾等一世也。

translations.literal: This again falls short of our generation.
translations.idiomatic: This too falls short of our generation.

sentences.zh: 吾今日不為貧賤，然居住舍宅，不作壯麗華飾者，正慮汝等後世不賢，不能保守之，將為勢家所奪。

translations.literal: I am not poor or lowly today, yet I do not make my dwelling splendid and ornate, precisely because I fear that if you later prove unworthy you will not be able to preserve it and it will be seized by powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: I am not poor today, yet I do not build a splendid house, precisely because I fear that if you prove unworthy in later generations you will not keep it and powerful families will seize it.

sentences.zh: 北都時，朝法嚴急。

translations.literal: In the days of the northern capital, court law was strict and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In the days of the northern capital, court law was harsh and exacting.

sentences.zh: 太和初，吾兄弟三人並居內職：兄在高祖左右，吾與津在文明太后左右。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe we three brothers all held inner posts: my elder brother at Emperor Gaozu's side, Jin and I at Empress Dowager Wenming's side.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era we three brothers all held posts within the palace: my elder brother at Emperor Gaozu's side, Jin and I at Empress Dowager Wenming's side.

sentences.zh: 于時口敕，責諸內官，十日仰密得一事，不列便大嗔嫌。

translations.literal: At that time by oral edict the inner officials were charged: within ten days you must secretly obtain one matter; if you do not report it, there will be great anger.
translations.idiomatic: By oral edict the inner officials were charged: within ten days each must secretly obtain one reportable matter; failure brought fierce reprimand.

sentences.zh: 諸人多有依敕密列者，亦有太后、高祖中間傳言構間者。

translations.literal: Many followed the edict and made secret reports; there were also those who passed words between the empress dowager and the emperor to sow discord.
translations.idiomatic: Many obeyed and filed secret reports; others passed words between the empress dowager and the emperor to sow discord.

sentences.zh: 吾兄弟自相誡曰：「今忝二聖近臣，居母之間難，宜深慎之。

translations.literal: We brothers admonished one another, saying, "We now disgracefully serve as close ministers to the Two Sages; to stand between mother and son is perilous and demands the deepest caution."
translations.idiomatic: We admonished one another: "We serve as close ministers to the Two Sages; to stand between mother and son is perilous and demands the deepest caution."

sentences.zh: 又列人事，亦何容易，縱被嗔責，勿輕言。

translations.literal: Moreover, to report on people's affairs is no easy thing; even if we are scolded, we must not speak lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Reporting on others is no light matter; even if we are scolded, we must not speak rashly."

sentences.zh: 」十餘年中，不嚐言一人罪過。

translations.literal: " For more than ten years we never once spoke of a single person's fault.
translations.idiomatic: " For more than ten years we never once denounced a single person's fault.

sentences.zh: 時大被嫌責，答曰：「臣等非不聞人語，正恐不審，仰誤聖聽，以是不敢言。

translations.literal: We were then greatly blamed and reproached and answered, "We your subjects are not deaf to people's talk; we only fear we may not judge correctly and mislead Your Sagely Hearing—therefore we dare not speak."
translations.idiomatic: When we were sharply rebuked we answered, "We are not deaf to men's talk; we only fear we may judge wrongly and mislead Your Sagely Hearing—that is why we dare not speak."

sentences.zh: 」於後終以不言。

translations.literal: " Afterward we were finally left in peace for not speaking.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end we were left in peace because we would not speak.

sentences.zh: 蒙賞及二聖間言語，終不敢輒爾傳通。

translations.literal: Though we received rewards, as for words between the Two Sages we never dared lightly to pass them on.
translations.idiomatic: Though we were rewarded, we never dared lightly to relay what passed between the Two Sages.

sentences.zh: 太和二十一年，吾從濟州來朝，在清徽堂豫宴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taihe I came to court from Jizhou and attended a preparatory banquet in the Qinghui Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Taihe I came to court from Jizhou and attended a banquet in the Qinghui Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂諸貴曰：「北京之日，太后嚴明，吾每得杖。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said to the assembled nobles, "In the days at the northern capital the empress dowager was strict and clear-sighted; I was often beaten with the staff."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu told the assembled nobles, "In the days at the northern capital the empress dowager was strict and clear-sighted; I was often beaten with the staff."

sentences.zh: 左右因此有是非言。

translations.literal: Those at my side therefore spread right-and-wrong talk.
translations.idiomatic: Those at my side therefore spread gossip between them.

sentences.zh: 和朕母子者，唯楊播兄弟。

translations.literal: Those who harmonized me, mother and son, were only the brothers Yang Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Only the brothers Yang Bo kept peace between my mother and me.

sentences.zh: 」遂舉爵賜兄及我酒。

translations.literal: " He then raised his goblet and bestowed wine on my elder brother and me.
translations.idiomatic: " He raised his goblet and bestowed wine on my elder brother and me.

sentences.zh: 汝等脫若萬一蒙明主知遇，宜深慎言語，不可輕論人惡也。

translations.literal: If by any chance you should meet with an enlightened lord's favor, you ought to be deeply cautious in speech and must not lightly discuss others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance you win an enlightened lord's favor, be deeply cautious in speech and never lightly discuss another man's faults.

sentences.zh: 吾自惟文武才藝、門望姻援不勝他人。

translations.literal: I myself consider that in civil and military talent, family standing, and marital connections I do not surpass others.
translations.idiomatic: I myself know that in civil and military talent, family standing, and marital connections I do not surpass others.

sentences.zh: 一旦位登侍中、尚書，四曆九卿，十為刺史，光祿大夫、儀同、開府、司徒、太保，津今復為司空者，正由忠謹慎口，不嚐論人之過，無貴無賤，待之以禮，以是故至此耳。

translations.literal: Once having ascended to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of the Masters of Writing, having passed through the Nine Ministers four times, having been regional inspector ten times, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Yitong, Commissioner with Full Staff, Minister over the Masses, and Grand Guardian — that Jin is again Minister of Works now is precisely because of loyalty, prudence, and cautious speech, never discussing people's faults, treating all without distinction of noble or base with courtesy; for these reasons he has reached this point, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Jin has risen to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of the Masters of Writing, served four times among the Nine Ministers, held ten regional inspectorates, and filled posts from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Yitong through Commissioner with Full Staff, Minister over the Masses, and Grand Guardian — and he is Minister of Works again today — solely because he is loyal, careful, and guarded in speech, never discusses others' faults, and treats everyone, high or low, with courtesy. That is how he came so far.

sentences.zh: 聞汝等學時俗人，乃有坐待客者，有驅馳勢門者，有輕論人惡者；

translations.literal: I hear that in studying you follow vulgar people, and so there are those who sit waiting for guests, those who drive urgently to the gates of powerful families, and those who lightly discuss people's evil;
translations.idiomatic: I hear that in your studies you imitate vulgar men: some sit idly waiting for callers, some rush to the gates of the powerful, and some speak lightly of others' faults;

sentences.zh: 及見貴勝則敬重之，見貧賤則慢易之，此人行之大失，立身之大病也。

translations.literal: When they see the noble and eminent they respect and honor them, when they see the poor and lowly they treat them with contempt and ease — this is a great failure in conduct and a great disease in establishing oneself.
translations.idiomatic: When they meet the powerful they show respect, and when they meet the poor they treat them with contempt — that is a grave moral failure and a fatal flaw in how a man conducts his life.

sentences.zh: 汝家仕皇魏以來，高祖以下乃有七郡太守、三十二州刺史，內外顯職，時流少比。

translations.literal: Since your family entered service under the Imperial Wei, from the High Ancestor down there have been seven commandery grand administrators and thirty-two regional inspectors, with prominent posts at court and abroad — few in the age can compare.
translations.idiomatic: Since your family entered imperial service under the Wei, from the time of the High Ancestor down there have been seven commandery administrators and thirty-two regional inspectors, with distinguished posts at court and in the provinces — few families of the age can match that record.

sentences.zh: 汝等若能存禮節，不為奢淫驕慢，假不勝人，足免尤誚，足成名家。

translations.literal: If you can preserve ritual and propriety and not indulge in extravagance, dissipation, arrogance, and insolence, even if you do not surpass others, that is enough to escape blame and reproach and enough to become an established family.
translations.idiomatic: If you can hold to proper conduct and avoid extravagance, dissipation, arrogance, and insolence, then even if you never surpass others you will still escape reproach and preserve the family's good name.

sentences.zh: 吾今年始七十五，自惟氣力，尚堪朝覲天子，所以孜孜求退者，正欲使汝等知天下滿足之議，為一門法耳，非是苟求千載之名。

translations.literal: I am only seventy-five this year; considering my strength, I am still able to attend court and pay homage to the Son of Heaven. The reason I earnestly seek retirement is precisely to make you know the principle of contentment under Heaven and establish it as a family rule — it is not that I seek a name to last a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: I am only seventy-five this year, and by my strength I could still attend court and pay homage to the emperor. I press so hard for retirement because I want you to learn the virtue of knowing when enough is enough and make that the rule of our house — not because I crave a name that will last a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 汝等能記吾言，吾百年後終無恨矣。

translations.literal: If you can remember my words, after my hundred years I will ultimately have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you remember what I have said, I shall have no regrets after I am gone.

sentences.zh: 椿還華陰。

translations.literal: Chun returned to Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Chun went back to Huayin.

sentences.zh: 逾年，為爾硃天光所害，時人莫不怨痛之。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was killed by Erzhu Tianguang, and people of the time all resented and grieved over it.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was killed by Erzhu Tianguang, and everyone at the time mourned and resented his death.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈太師、丞相、都督、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taichang era, he was posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor, Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief, and Regional Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Chancellor, Commander-in-Chief, and Regional Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 子昱。

translations.literal: His son was Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Yu.

sentences.zh: 昱字元略，起家廣平王懷左常侍。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Yuanlue, began his career as Left Regular Attendant to Prince Huai of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, whose courtesy name was Yuanlue, began his career as Left Regular Attendant to Prince Huai of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 懷好武事，數遊獵，昱每規諫。

translations.literal: Huai loved military affairs and frequently went out hunting; Yu repeatedly admonished and remonstrated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai loved military affairs and often went hunting, and Yu repeatedly remonstrated with him.

sentences.zh: 正始中，以京兆、廣平二王國臣多縱恣，詔御史中尉崔亮窮案之，伏法都市者三十餘人，不死者悉除名，唯昱與博陵崔楷以忠諫免。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, because the retainers of the two princely establishments of Jingzhao and Guangping were largely unrestrained and willful, an edict ordered the Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang to investigate thoroughly; more than thirty were executed in the capital market, those not put to death were all struck from the rolls, and only Yu and Cui Kai of Boling were exempted on account of loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengshi era, because the retainers of the Jingzhao and Guangping princely establishments had grown lawless, the court ordered Censor-in-Chief Cui Liang to investigate. More than thirty men were executed in the capital market, the rest were dismissed from office, and only Yu and Cui Kai of Boling were spared because their loyal remonstrance had been noted.

sentences.zh: 後除太學博士、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書令王肅除揚州刺史，出頓洛陽東亭。

translations.literal: Initially, when Minister of the Masters of Writing Wang Su was appointed Regional Inspector of Yang Province, on departing he halted at the Eastern Pavilion of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Wang Su, Minister of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Regional Inspector of Yang Province, he paused on his way out at the Eastern Pavilion of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 酣後，廣陽王嘉、北海王詳等與播論議競理，播不為屈。

translations.literal: After becoming drunk, Prince Jia of Guangyang, Prince Xiang of Beihai, and others debated principles with Bo in competitive argument, and Bo was not made to yield.
translations.idiomatic: After the wine had gone around, Prince Jia of Guangyang, Prince Xiang of Beihai, and others argued doctrine with Yang Bo, but Bo would not be beaten.

sentences.zh: 北海王顧昱曰：「尊伯性剛不伏理，大不如尊使君也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Beihai turned to Yu and said, "Your honored uncle's nature is stiff and will not submit to reason — greatly inferior to your honored father as regional inspector."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Beihai turned to Yu and said, "Your uncle's temper is so unyielding that he will not bow to reason — nothing like your father when he was regional inspector."

sentences.zh: 」昱對曰：「昱父道隆則從其隆，道洿則從其洿；

translations.literal: Yu replied, "When my father's way is lofty, Yu follows its loftiness; when the way is low, Yu follows its lowness;"
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "When my father's way is lofty, I follow its loftiness; when it is low, I follow its lowness;"

sentences.zh: 伯父剛則不吐，柔亦不茹。

translations.literal: "my uncle, if stiff, will not spit it out, if soft, will not swallow it either."
translations.idiomatic: "my uncle, if the matter is hard he will not spit it out, and if it is soft he will not swallow it either."

sentences.zh: 」坐歎其能言。

translations.literal: Those present sighed in admiration at his ability to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Those seated there all sighed in admiration at how well he spoke.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「非此郎，何得申二父之美。」

translations.literal: Su said, "Without this young man, how could the excellence of the two fathers be expressed?"
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Without this young man, how could the virtues of the two fathers ever have been brought out?"

sentences.zh: 延昌三年，以本官帶詹事丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yan-chang, with his original office he additionally served as Assistant to the Household Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yan-chang era he retained his original post while also serving as Assistant to the Household Mentor.

sentences.zh: 時明帝在懷抱中，至於出入，左右、乳母而已，不令宮寮聞知。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming was still in swaddling clothes; as for going in and out, there were only attendants at his side and wet nurses — the palace staff were not allowed to know.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Ming was still an infant in arms, and when he went in and out of the palace only his attendants and wet nurses accompanied him; the palace staff were kept from knowing.

sentences.zh: 昱諫曰：「陛下不以臣等凡淺，備位宮臣，太子動止，宜令翼從。

translations.literal: Yu remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty does not regard us as common and shallow, and has installed us as palace officials; the crown prince's movements and stops ought to be made to have attendants following at his side."
translations.idiomatic: Yu remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty, not considering us unworthy, has appointed us as palace officials, so the crown prince's comings and goings ought to be attended by us."

sentences.zh: 自比以來，輕爾出入，進無二傅導引之美，退闕群寮陪侍之式。

translations.literal: From this time on he has lightly gone in and out; on going forth there is none of the excellence of the two tutors' guidance, on returning there lacks the formality of the assembled officials' attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Since then he has come and gone too casually: when he goes out he lacks the proper guidance of the two tutors, and when he returns he lacks the formal attendance of the assembled officials.

sentences.zh: 非所謂示人軌儀，著君臣之義。

translations.literal: This is not what is called showing people proper standards and making clear the meaning of ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: This is not the way to display proper conduct to the world or to make the relation between ruler and minister clear.

sentences.zh: 陛下若召太子，必降手敕，令臣下咸知，為後世法。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty summons the crown prince, you must issue a handwritten edict so that the officials all know, and make it a model for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty summons the crown prince, you should issue a handwritten edict so that all officials know of it and so that later ages may have a precedent.

sentences.zh: 」於是詔自今若非手敕，勿令兒輒出，宮臣在直者，從至萬歲門。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict declared that from now on, unless there is a handwritten edict, the child must not be allowed to go out at will, and palace officials on duty are to follow him as far as the Gate of Ten Thousand Years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: from that time forward the child was not to leave the palace unless there was a handwritten order, and the palace officials on duty were to accompany him as far as the Gate of Ten Thousand Years.

sentences.zh: 轉太尉掾，兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a clerk in the Ministry of War and concurrently served as Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to a clerkship in the Ministry of War and concurrently served as Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 靈太后嘗謂昱曰：「親姻在外，不稱人心，卿有所聞，慎勿諱隱。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling once said to Yu, "Relatives by marriage outside the court do not accord with people's hearts; if you hear anything, be careful not to conceal it."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling once told Yu, "Some of our relatives by marriage in the provinces are unpopular. If you hear anything, do not hide it from me."

sentences.zh: 」昱奏揚州刺史李崇五車載貨，恆州刺史楊鈞造銀食器十具，並餉領軍元叉。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized that Regional Inspector Li Chong of Yang Province loaded five carts with goods, and Regional Inspector Yang Jun of Heng Province made ten sets of silver tableware, both presenting them to the Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reported that Li Chong, Regional Inspector of Yang Province, had sent five cartloads of goods, and Yang Jun, Regional Inspector of Heng Province, had made ten sets of silver tableware, both as gifts to the Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha.

sentences.zh: 靈太后令召叉夫妻，泣而責之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered Yuan Cha and his wife summoned and, weeping, reproached them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling had Yuan Cha and his wife summoned and rebuked them through her tears.

sentences.zh: 叉深恨昱。

translations.literal: Cha deeply hated Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Cha came to hate Yu deeply.

sentences.zh: 昱第六叔舒妻，武昌王和之妹，和即叉之從祖父。

translations.literal: The wife of Yu's sixth uncle Shu was the younger sister of Prince He of Wuchang, and He was Cha's father's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Yu's sixth uncle Shu was the sister of Prince He of Wuchang, who was Cha's grand-uncle.

sentences.zh: 舒早喪，有一男六女，及終喪，元氏請別居。

translations.literal: Shu died early, leaving one son and six daughters; when the mourning period ended, the Yuan clan requested separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had died young, leaving one son and six daughters, and when the mourning period ended the Yuan clanswoman asked to set up a separate household.

sentences.zh: 昱父椿集親姻泣謂曰：「我弟不幸早終，今男未婚，女未嫁，何便求別居？

translations.literal: Yu's father Chun gathered the relatives and, weeping, said, "My younger brother unfortunately died early; now the son is unmarried and the daughters are unbetrothed — how can you immediately seek separate residence?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu's father Chun gathered the relatives and said through his tears, "My brother died too young. The boy is still unmarried and the girls are still unbetrothed — how can you ask to live apart so soon?"

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: He did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 遂懷憾。

translations.literal: Thereupon they harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年，瀛州人劉宣明謀反，事覺逃竄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Sheng-gui, Liu Xuanming of Ying Province plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered he fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Sheng-gui era, Liu Xuanming of Ying Province plotted rebellion, and when the plot was discovered he fled.

sentences.zh: 叉使和及元氏誣告昱藏宣明，雲昱父椿、叔津並送甲仗三百具，謀圖不逞。

translations.literal: Cha had He and the Yuan clanswoman falsely accuse Yu of hiding Xuanming, saying that Yu's father Chun and his uncle Jin had both sent three hundred sets of armor and weapons in a plot that did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Cha had Prince He and the Yuan clanswoman falsely accuse Yu of harboring Xuanming, claiming that Yu's father Chun and his uncle Jin had each sent three hundred sets of arms and armor in support of a failed plot.

sentences.zh: 叉又構成其事。

translations.literal: Cha further fabricated the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Cha then built the case further.

sentences.zh: 乃遣夜圍昱宅收之，並無所獲。

translations.literal: He then sent men by night to surround Yu's residence and arrest him, but nothing was found.
translations.idiomatic: Men were sent by night to surround Yu's house and arrest him, but nothing incriminating was found.

sentences.zh: 太后問狀。

translations.literal: The empress dowager questioned the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager questioned him about the case.

sentences.zh: 昱具對元氏構釁之端，言至哀切。

translations.literal: Yu fully answered regarding the beginnings of the Yuan clanswoman's provocation, his words extremely sorrowful and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gave a full account of how the Yuan clanswoman had provoked the quarrel, speaking with deep sorrow and urgency.

sentences.zh: 太后乃解昱縛，和及元氏並處死刑。

translations.literal: The empress dowager then released Yu from his bonds, and both He and the Yuan clanswoman were sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager then had Yu unbound, and both Prince He and the Yuan clanswoman were sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 而叉相左右，和直免官，元氏卒亦不坐。

translations.literal: But Cha was at her side, so He was merely stripped of office, and the Yuan clanswoman in the end was not punished either.
translations.idiomatic: But because Cha stood at the empress dowager's side, He was merely dismissed from office and the Yuan clanswoman was never punished in the end.

sentences.zh: 及叉之廢太后也，乃出昱為濟陰內史。
