translations.literal: When Cha deposed the empress dowager, Yu was then sent out to be Internal Administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha deposed the empress dowager, Yu was sent out to serve as Internal Administrator of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 中山王熙起兵於鄴，叉遣黃門盧同詣鄴刑熙，並窮黨與。

translations.literal: Prince Xi of Zhongshan raised troops at Ye; Cha dispatched the Yellow Gate official Lu Tong to Ye to execute Xi and thoroughly pursue his associates.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xi of Zhongshan raised troops at Ye, Cha sent the Yellow Gate official Lu Tong to Ye to execute Xi and root out his associates.

sentences.zh: 同希叉旨，就郡鎖昱赴鄴，囚訊百日乃還任。

translations.literal: Tong, hoping to please Cha's intent, went to the commandery, put Yu in fetters, and took him to Ye; after a hundred days of imprisonment and interrogation he was returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Eager to please Cha, Tong went to the commandery, put Yu in chains, and took him to Ye, where he was imprisoned and interrogated for a hundred days before being sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，除中書侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiao-chang, he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xiao-chang era he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 後賊圍豳州，詔昱兼侍中，持節催西北道大都督、北海王顥，仍隨軍監察。

translations.literal: Later, when bandits besieged Bin Prefecture, an edict made Yu concurrently Attendant-in-Ordinary, bearing the staff of office to urge on the Great Commander of the Northwest Route, Prince Hao of Beihai, and he continued with the army as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when rebels besieged Bin Prefecture, Yu was made concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary and sent with imperial credentials to hurry Prince Hao of Beihai, Great Commander of the Northwest Route, while accompanying the army as inspector.

sentences.zh: 豳州圍解。

translations.literal: The siege of Bin Prefecture was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Bin Prefecture was lifted.

sentences.zh: 雍州蜀賊張映龍、姜神達知州內虛，謀欲攻掩。

translations.literal: The Shu bandits Zhang Yinglong and Jiang Shenda of Yong Province, knowing the province was empty within, plotted to attack by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu rebels Zhang Yinglong and Jiang Shenda in Yong Province, seeing that the province was undefended, planned a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 刺史元修義懼而請援，一日一夜，書移九通。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector Yuan Xiuyi, in fear, requested reinforcements; in one day and one night he sent nine dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector Yuan Xiuyi, alarmed, called for help and sent nine dispatches in a single day and night.

sentences.zh: 都督李叔仁遲疑不赴。

translations.literal: Commander Li Shuren hesitated and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Li Shuren hesitated and would not march.

sentences.zh: 昱曰：「若長安不守，大軍自然瓦散，此軍雖往，有何益也。

translations.literal: Yu said, "If Chang'an is not held, the great army will naturally scatter like broken tiles; even if this army goes, what benefit will there be?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "If Chang'an falls, the main army will collapse of its own accord. Even if we march, what good will it do?"

sentences.zh: 」遂與叔仁等俱進，於陣斬神達，諸賊迸散。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced together with Shuren and the others, beheaded Shenda in battle, and the bandits all scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced with Shuren and the others, killed Shenda in battle, and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔以昱受旨催督，而顥軍稽緩，遂免昱官。

translations.literal: An edict held that although Yu had received orders to urge and supervise, Hao's army had been slow, and so Yu's office was removed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict blamed Yu for having received orders to hurry the campaign while Hao's army moved too slowly, and Yu was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋除涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Regional Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Regional Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 未幾，昱父椿為雍州，征昱除吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Before long, when Yu's father Chun took Yong Province, Yu was summoned and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when Yu's father Chun became governor of Yong Province, Yu was recalled and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及蕭寶夤等敗於關中，以昱兼七兵尚書、持節、假撫軍、都督，防守雍州。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin and others were defeated in Guanzhong, Yu was made concurrently Minister of the Seven Arms, bearing the staff of office, acting General Who Pacifies the Army, and Commander to defend Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Baoyin and the others were defeated in Guanzhong, Yu was made concurrent Minister of the Seven Arms, given imperial credentials, named acting General Who Pacifies the Army, and put in command of the defense of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 昱遇賊失利而返。

translations.literal: Yu encountered bandits, suffered defeat, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yu met the rebels, was defeated, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後除鎮東將軍、假車騎將軍、東南道都督，又加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commander of the Southeast Route, and was further given Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed General Who Pacifies the East, acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander of the Southeast Route, and was also given the post of Regular Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 於後太山守羊侃據郡南叛，侃兄深時為徐州行台，府州咸欲禁深。

translations.literal: Afterward the Administrator of Taishan, Yang Kan, held the commandery and rebelled in the south; Kan's elder brother Shen was then at the Xuzhou field office, and the prefecture and province all wished to detain Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Kan, Administrator of Taishan, rebelled while holding the commandery in the south. His elder brother Shen was then at the Xuzhou field headquarters, and officials in the prefecture and province all wanted to detain him.

sentences.zh: 昱曰：「昔叔向不以鮒也見廢，奈何以侃罪深，宜呼朝旨。

translations.literal: Yu said, "In old times Shu Xiang was not dismissed because of Fuyu — how can we punish Shen for Kan's crime? The court's intent should be summoned."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "In antiquity Shu Xiang was not dismissed because of his son Fuyu. How can we punish Shen for Kan's crime? We should wait for the court's decision."

sentences.zh: 」不許群議。

translations.literal: He did not permit the assembled discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He would not allow the proposal to stand.

sentences.zh: 還朝未幾，元顥侵逼大梁，除昱南道大都督，鎮滎陽。

translations.literal: Not long after returning to court, when Yuan Hao pressed upon Daliang, Yu was appointed Great Commander of the Southern Route and stationed at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he returned to court, Yuan Hao pressed toward Daliang, and Yu was made Great Commander of the Southern Route and stationed at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 顥禽濟陰王暉業，乘虛徑進，城陷。

translations.literal: Hao captured Prince Ye of Jiyin, seized the opening to advance directly, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Hao captured Prince Ye of Jiyin, exploited the opening to advance straight on the city, and Xingyang fell.

sentences.zh: 昱與弟息五人在門樓上。

translations.literal: Yu and five younger brothers and sons were on the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was on the gate tower with five younger brothers and sons.

sentences.zh: 顥至，執昱下，責曰：「卿今死甘心不？

translations.literal: When Hao arrived, he seized Yu and brought him down, reproaching him: "Do you now accept death willingly?"
translations.idiomatic: When Hao arrived, he had Yu seized and brought down from the tower and demanded, "Are you willing to die now?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「分不望生，向所以不下樓，正慮亂兵耳。

translations.literal: He answered, "By my lot I do not hope to live; the reason I did not come down earlier was precisely that I feared the disorderly soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I never expected to live. I stayed on the tower only because I feared what the disorderly soldiers might do."

sentences.zh: 但恨八十老父無人供養，乞小弟一命，便是死不朽也。

translations.literal: I only regret that my eighty-year-old father has no one to support him; I beg the life of my youngest brother — that would be death without perishing.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that my eighty-year-old father will have no one to care for him. Spare my youngest brother's life, and my death will not have been in vain.

sentences.zh: 」顥將陳慶之、胡光等伏顥帳前曰：「陛下度江三千里，無遺鏃費。

translations.literal: Hao's generals Chen Qingzhi, Hu Guang, and others prostrated themselves before Hao's tent and said, "Your Majesty crossed the river three thousand li without wasting a single arrow."
translations.idiomatic: Hao's generals Chen Qingzhi, Hu Guang, and others prostrated themselves before his tent and said, "Your Majesty crossed the Yangzi three thousand li without wasting a single arrow."

sentences.zh: 昨日殺傷五百餘人，求乞楊昱以快意。

translations.literal: Yesterday more than five hundred were killed and wounded; we beg Yang Yu to satisfy our pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday more than five hundred men were killed and wounded. We ask that Yang Yu be given to us so that we may have our satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 」景曰：「我在江東聞梁主言，初下都，袁昂為吳郡不降，稱其忠節。

translations.literal: Jing said, "When I was in Jiangdong I heard the Liang ruler say that when he first descended on the capital, Yuan Ang as Administrator of Wu Commandery did not surrender, and he praised his loyalty and integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "When I was in the southeast I heard the Liang emperor say that when he first entered the capital, Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wu Commandery, refused to surrender, and he praised his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 奈何殺昱。

translations.literal: How can we kill Yu?
translations.idiomatic: How then can we kill Yu?

sentences.zh: 」於是斬昱下統帥三十七人，皆令蜀兵刳腹取心食之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the thirty-seven commanders subordinate to Yu were beheaded, and all were made to have their bellies cut open and hearts taken out by Shu soldiers to be eaten.
translations.idiomatic: The thirty-seven commanders under Yu were then beheaded, and Shu soldiers were ordered to cut open their bellies, take out their hearts, and eat them.

sentences.zh: 孝莊還，復前官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned, his former offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to power, Yu was restored to his former offices.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之死，昱為東道行台拒爾硃仲遠。

translations.literal: At the death of Erzhu Rong, Yu served on the Eastern Route field staff to resist Erzhu Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Yu served on the Eastern Route field staff to hold off Erzhu Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 會爾硃兆入洛，昱還京師。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Yu returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao took Luoyang, Yu went back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，亦為天光所害。

translations.literal: Later, when he returned to his home district, he was also killed by Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after he returned home, he too was killed by Erzhu Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈司空公、定州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously awarded Duke of the Ministry of Works and Regional Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as Duke of the Ministry of Works and Regional Inspector of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子孝邕，員外郎，奔免。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoyong, a Supernumerary Gentleman, fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoyong, a Supernumerary Gentleman, fled and escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 匿蠻中，潛結渠率，謀報爾硃氏。

translations.literal: He hid among the barbarians, secretly joined with tribal chiefs, and plotted to avenge himself on the Erzhu clan.
translations.idiomatic: He hid among the tribal peoples, secretly rallied local chiefs, and plotted revenge against the Erzhu family.

sentences.zh: 微服入洛，為爾硃世隆所殺。

translations.literal: Disguised in common clothes he entered Luoyang and was killed by Erzhu Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Luoyang in disguise and was killed by Erzhu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 椿弟穎，字惠哲，本州別駕。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Ying, styled Huizhe, was Vice Administrator of the native province.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Ying, whose courtesy name was Huizhe, served as Vice Administrator of the province.

sentences.zh: 穎弟順，字延和，寬裕謹厚。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Shun, styled Yanhe, was generous, tolerant, prudent, and solid.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Shun, whose courtesy name was Yanhe, was generous, prudent, and solid in character.

sentences.zh: 豫立莊帝功，封三門縣伯，位冀州刺史。

translations.literal: For the merit of establishing Emperor Zhuang in advance, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Sanmen County and reached the post of Regional Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: For helping to establish Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Sanmen County and rose to Regional Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 罷州還，遇害。

translations.literal: When he left the province and returned, he met with violent death.
translations.idiomatic: After he left his post and returned home, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈太尉公、錄尚書事、相州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously awarded Duke of the Ministry of War, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Regional Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as Duke of the Ministry of War, Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Regional Inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 子辯，字僧達，位東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Bian, styled Sengda, held the post of Regional Inspector of Eastern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bian, whose courtesy name was Sengda, served as Regional Inspector of Eastern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 辯弟仲宣，有風度才學。

translations.literal: Bian's younger brother Zhongxuan had bearing, talent, and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's younger brother Zhongxuan had fine bearing, talent, and learning.

sentences.zh: 位正平太守，爵恆農伯，在郡有能名。

translations.literal: He held the post of Administrator of Zhengping, was ennobled as Baron of Hengnong, and in the commandery had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Zhengping, was ennobled as Baron of Hengnong, and earned a reputation for competence in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 還京，兄弟與父同遇害。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital, the brothers met violent death together with their father.
translations.idiomatic: After they returned to the capital, the brothers were killed together with their father.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，辯贈儀同三司、恆州刺史；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, Bian was posthumously awarded Yitong with the Three Excellencies and Regional Inspector of Heng Province;
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taichang era Bian was posthumously honored with Yitong rank equal to the Three Excellencies and as Regional Inspector of Heng Province;

sentences.zh: 仲宣贈尚書右僕射、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Regional Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Regional Inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 仲宣子玄就，幼而俊拔。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan's son Xuanjiu was from youth outstanding and exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan's son Xuanjiu was precocious and exceptionally gifted.

sentences.zh: 收捕時，年九歲，牽挽兵人曰：「欲害諸尊，乞先就死。

translations.literal: At the time of the arrest, he was nine years old; tugging at the soldiers he said, "If you wish to harm my elders, I beg to die first."
translations.idiomatic: When the arrests were made he was nine years old. Pulling at the soldiers he said, "If you mean to harm my elders, let me die first."

sentences.zh: 」兵以刀斫斷其臂，猶請死不止，遂先殺之。

translations.literal: A soldier cut off his arm with a blade, yet he still begged to die without stopping, and so they killed him first.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier hacked off his arm with a blade, but he still kept begging to die, so they killed him first.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，贈汝陰太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, he was posthumously awarded Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yongxi era he was posthumously honored as Administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 順弟津。

translations.literal: Shun's younger brother Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's younger brother was Jin.

sentences.zh: 津字羅漢，本字延祚，孝文賜改焉。

translations.literal: Jin, styled Luohan, originally styled Yanzuo, was granted a change by Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, whose courtesy name was Luohan, had originally been styled Yanzuo; Emperor Xiaowen granted him the new name.

sentences.zh: 少端謹，以器度見稱。

translations.literal: From youth he was upright and careful, and was praised for his bearing and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was upright and careful, and won praise for his bearing and capacity.

sentences.zh: 年十一，除侍御中散。

translations.literal: At age eleven he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 時孝文幼沖，文明太后臨朝，津曾入侍左右，忽咳逆失聲，遂吐血數升，藏之衣袖。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowen was young, and Empress Dowager Wenming held court; Jin once entered to attend at the emperor's side, suddenly suffered a coughing fit and lost his voice, then spat up several sheng of blood and hid it in his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was still a child and Empress Dowager Wenming held court. Once while attending at the emperor's side, Jin suddenly suffered a violent coughing fit, lost his voice, and spat up several sheng of blood, which he concealed in his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 太后聞聲，閱而不見，問其故，具以實言，遂以敬慎見知。

translations.literal: The empress dowager heard the sound, investigated but saw nothing, asked the reason, and he fully told the truth; thus he became known for reverence and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager heard the sound, looked but saw nothing, and asked what had happened. He told her the whole truth, and from that time he was recognized for reverence and prudence.

sentences.zh: 賜縑百匹，遷符璽郎中。

translations.literal: He was granted one hundred bolts of silk and transferred to Gentleman of the Seals and Tallies.
translations.idiomatic: He received one hundred bolts of silk as a reward and was promoted to Gentleman of the Seals and Tallies.

sentences.zh: 津以身在禁密，不外交遊，至宗族姻表罕相參侯。

translations.literal: Because Jin's position was in the inner confidential service, he did not socialize abroad, and even with clan and affinal kin he rarely paid visits or inquired after them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jin served in the palace's inner confidential ranks, he did not socialize outside court, and even with clan and affinal kin he rarely paid calls.

sentences.zh: 司徒馮誕與津少結交友，而津見其貴寵，每恆退避，及相招命，多辭疾不往。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Feng Dan had formed a friendship with Jin in youth, but Jin, seeing his noble favor, constantly kept his distance; when invited and summoned, he often pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Feng Dan had been Jin's friend since youth, but Jin, seeing how favored and powerful he had become, constantly kept his distance; when Feng summoned him, he often pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 誕以為恨，而津逾遠焉。

translations.literal: Dan took this as a grievance, while Jin kept himself ever more distant.
translations.idiomatic: Dan resented this, and Jin kept himself ever more aloof.

sentences.zh: 人或謂之曰：「司徒，君之少舊，何自外也？

translations.literal: Someone said to him, "The Minister over the Masses is your old friend from youth — why treat him as an outsider?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "The Minister over the Masses is an old friend of yours — why keep him at arm's length?"

sentences.zh: 」津曰：「為勢家所厚，復何容易！

translations.literal: Jin said, "To be favored by a powerful house — how could that be easy!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin replied, "When a powerful house favors you, nothing comes easily!"

sentences.zh: 但全吾今日，亦足矣。

translations.literal: Merely to preserve myself as I am today is already enough.
translations.idiomatic: Simply to preserve myself as I am today is enough.

sentences.zh: 」轉振威將軍，領監曹奏事令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Quells Might and concurrently served as Director of Memorials in the Supervisory Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Quells Might and concurrently appointed Director of Memorials in the Supervisory Bureau.

sentences.zh: 孝文南征，以津為都督、征南府長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen marched south on campaign, Jin was made Area Commander and Chief Clerk of the Southern Expedition Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen marched south on campaign, Jin was appointed area commander and chief clerk of the southern expedition headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後遷長水校尉，仍直閣。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Colonel of the Long River and continued to serve in the Direct Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Colonel of the Long River while continuing to serve in the Direct Attendance.

sentences.zh: 景明中，宣武游於北芒，津時陪從。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era, Emperor Xuanwu toured at Beimang, and Jin at the time accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingming era Emperor Xuanwu toured Beimang, and Jin accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 太尉、咸陽王禧謀反，帝馳入華林。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant and Prince of Xianyang, Xi, plotted rebellion; the emperor galloped into the Hualin Park.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant and Prince of Xianyang, Xi, plotted rebellion, and the emperor galloped into Hualin Park.

sentences.zh: 時直閣中有同禧謀，皆在從限。

translations.literal: At that time among those in the Direct Attendance were some who shared Xi's plot, all within the entourage limits.
translations.idiomatic: At that time some members of the Direct Attendance had joined Xi's plot, and all were within the imperial entourage.

sentences.zh: 及禧平，帝顧謂朝臣曰：「直閣半為逆黨，非至忠者安能不豫此謀。

translations.literal: When Xi was suppressed, the emperor turned and said to the court ministers, "Half the Direct Attendance were rebels — only the most loyal could have avoided this conspiracy."
translations.idiomatic: After Xi was suppressed, the emperor turned to the court ministers and said, "Half the Direct Attendance were rebels — only the most loyal could have stayed clear of this plot."

sentences.zh: 」因拜津左中郎將，遷驍騎將軍，仍直閣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jin was appointed Left Commandant of the Palace Guard, transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry, and continued in the Direct Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Jin Left Commandant of the Palace Guard, promoted him to General of Valiant Cavalry, and kept him in the Direct Attendance.

sentences.zh: 出除岐州刺史，津巨細躬親，孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed Regional Inspector of Qi Province; Jin personally attended to every detail, never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Regional Inspector of Qi Province and personally attended to every detail without slackening.

sentences.zh: 有武功人齎絹三匹，去城十里，為賊所劫。

translations.literal: A man of Wugong was carrying three bolts of silk; ten li from the city he was robbed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: A man from Wugong was carrying three bolts of silk when, ten li from the city, he was robbed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 時有使者馳驛而至，被劫人因以告之。

translations.literal: At that time a messenger arrived by post-horse relay, and the robbed man therefore told him.
translations.idiomatic: A courier happened to arrive by post relay, and the robbed man told him what had happened.

sentences.zh: 使者到州，以狀白津。

translations.literal: The messenger reached the province and reported the matter to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When the courier reached the province he reported the matter to Jin.

sentences.zh: 津乃下教，雲有人著某色衣，乘某色馬，在城東十里被殺，不知姓名。

translations.literal: Jin then issued an order saying that someone wearing a certain-colored garment and riding a certain-colored horse had been killed ten li east of the city, his name unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then issued an order stating that someone wearing a certain-colored garment and riding a certain-colored horse had been killed ten li east of the city, identity unknown.

sentences.zh: 若有家人，可速收視。

translations.literal: If there were family members, they should quickly come to claim and view the body.
translations.idiomatic: If any family member recognized him, they should come at once to claim the body.

sentences.zh: 有一老母行哭而出，雲是己子。

translations.literal: An old woman came out weeping as she walked, saying it was her son.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman came out weeping, saying the victim was her son.

sentences.zh: 於是遣騎追收，並絹俱獲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent horsemen in pursuit to capture them, and both the robbers and the silk were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent horsemen in pursuit, and both the robbers and the silk were recovered.

sentences.zh: 自是闔境畏服。

translations.literal: From then on the whole jurisdiction feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the whole jurisdiction feared and submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 至於守令寮佐有濁貨者，未曾公言其罪，常以私書切責之。

translations.literal: As for prefects, magistrates, and staff assistants who had corrupt gains, he never publicly declared their crimes, but always rebuked them sharply in private letters.
translations.idiomatic: When prefects, magistrates, or staff assistants had taken corrupt gains, he never publicly denounced them but always rebuked them sharply in private letters.

sentences.zh: 於是官屬感厲，莫有犯法者。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officials were moved and inspired, and none violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: The officials were moved by this, and none dared break the law.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，起為華州刺史，與兄播前後牧本州，當世榮之。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanchang he was recalled as Regional Inspector of Hua Province; he and his elder brother Bo successively governed their native province, and the age honored this.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yanchang era he was recalled as Regional Inspector of Hua Province. He and his elder brother Bo had successively governed their native province, and their contemporaries regarded this as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 先是，受調絹度尺特長，在事因緣，共相進退，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: Previously, in collecting tax silk the measuring rod had been made especially long; officials took advantage of one another, advancing and retreating together, and the common people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, officials collecting tax silk had used extra-long measuring rods, colluding with one another to squeeze the people, who suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 津乃令依公尺度其輸物，尤好者賜以杯酒而出；

translations.literal: Jin then ordered that deliveries be measured by the standard public rod; those of especially fine quality he rewarded with a cup of wine before dismissing them;
translations.idiomatic: Jin ordered that all deliveries be measured by the standard public rod. Those of especially fine quality he rewarded with a cup of wine before sending them on their way;

sentences.zh: 其所輸少劣者，為受之，但無酒以示其恥。

translations.literal: those who delivered goods somewhat inferior he still accepted, but gave no wine to show their shame.
translations.idiomatic: those who delivered inferior goods he still accepted, but gave no wine, shaming them by the omission.

sentences.zh: 於是競相勸厲，官調更勝。

translations.literal: Thereupon they competed in encouraging one another, and the official levy improved still further.
translations.idiomatic: People then competed to improve their deliveries, and the official levy rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，北鎮擾亂，侵逼舊京，乃加津安北將軍，北道大都督，尋轉左衛，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang, the northern garrisons were in turmoil and pressed upon the old capital; Jin was then given the additional titles of General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Area Commander of the Northern Route; soon he was transferred to the Left Guard and given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era the northern garrisons fell into turmoil and threatened the old capital. Jin was given the additional titles of General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Area Commander of the Northern Route, then transferred to the Left Guard with the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 津始受命，出據靈丘。

translations.literal: When Jin first received his commission, he went out and took position at Lingqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin first received his commission he marched out and took position at Lingqiu.

sentences.zh: 而賊帥鮮于修禮起於博陵，定州危急，遂回師南赴。

translations.literal: But the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli rose at Boling, Ding Province was in grave peril, and so he turned his army south to go to its aid.
translations.idiomatic: But the rebel leader Xianyu Xiuli rose at Boling, Ding Province was in grave peril, and Jin turned his army south to its relief.

sentences.zh: 始至城下，榮壘未立，而州軍新敗。

translations.literal: When he first reached the city walls, the camp fortifications were not yet established, and the provincial army had just been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When he first reached the city, his camp fortifications were not yet in place and the provincial army had just suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 津以賊既乘勝，士眾榮疲，柵壘未安，不可擬敵，欲移軍入城，更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Jin, considering that the bandits were riding their victory, the troops were weary, and the palisades and fortifications were not secure, felt they could not match the enemy; he wished to move the army into the city and plan another effort later.
translations.idiomatic: Jin judged that the rebels were riding their victory, his troops were exhausted, and his defenses were not yet secure, so he could not meet the enemy in the field. He wanted to move his army into the city and plan his next move.

sentences.zh: 刺史元固稱賊既逼城，不可示弱，乃閉門不內。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector Yuan Gu said that since the bandits were already pressing the city, one must not show weakness, and so closed the gates and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector Yuan Gu argued that with the rebels already at the walls they must not show weakness, and closed the gates, refusing to admit them.

sentences.zh: 津揮刃欲斬門者，軍乃得入。

translations.literal: Jin waved his blade intending to cut down the gatekeepers, and only then did the army gain entry.
translations.idiomatic: Jin raised his blade as if to strike the gatekeepers, and only then was his army admitted.

sentences.zh: 賊果夜至，見柵空而去。

translations.literal: The bandits indeed came by night, saw the palisades empty, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came by night, found the camp abandoned, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其後，賊攻州城東面，已入羅城。

translations.literal: Afterward the bandits attacked the eastern face of the provincial city and had already entered the outer enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rebels attacked the eastern side of the provincial city and broke into the outer enclosure.

sentences.zh: 刺史閉小城東門，城中騷擾。

translations.literal: The regional inspector closed the small eastern gate of the inner city, and turmoil broke out within the city.
translations.idiomatic: The regional inspector closed the inner city's eastern gate, and panic spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 津開門出戰，賊退，人心少安。

translations.literal: Jin opened the gate and went out to fight; the bandits retreated, and the people's hearts were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin opened the gate and sallied forth; the rebels retreated and the people's spirits steadied somewhat.

sentences.zh: 尋除定州刺史，又兼吏部尚書、北道行台。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Regional Inspector of Ding Province and concurrently Minister of the Masters of Writing and Northern Route Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Regional Inspector of Ding Province while also serving as Minister of the Masters of Writing and head of the Northern Route Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，津兄椿得罪此州，由钜鹿人趙略投書所致。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jin's elder brother Chun had been condemned in this province because Zhao Lue of Julu had submitted a letter denouncing him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jin's elder brother Chun had fallen afoul of this province because Zhao Lue of Julu had submitted a denunciatory letter.

sentences.zh: 及津至，略舉家逃走。

translations.literal: When Jin arrived, Lue fled with his whole household.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin arrived, Lue fled with his entire household.

sentences.zh: 津乃下教慰喻，令其還業。

translations.literal: Jin then issued an order of reassurance and persuasion, ordering them to return to their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Jin issued a reassuring proclamation and told them to return to their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 於是闔州愧服，遠近稱之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the whole province felt ashamed and submitted; near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The whole province was shamed into submission, and people near and far praised him.

sentences.zh: 時賊帥鮮于修禮、杜洛周賤掠州境，孤城獨立，在兩寇之間。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chiefs Xianyu Xiuli and Du Luozhou plundered the province's borders; the isolated city stood alone between two invaders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebel leaders Xianyu Xiuli and Du Luozhou ravaged the province, and the isolated city stood alone between two enemy forces.

sentences.zh: 津修理戰具，更營雉堞。

translations.literal: Jin repaired the war equipment and again built the battlements.
translations.idiomatic: Jin repaired the war equipment and rebuilt the battlements.

sentences.zh: 又於城中去城十步，掘地至泉，廣作地道，潛兵湧出，置爐鑄鐵，持以灌賊。

translations.literal: He also dug ten paces inside the city wall down to the water table, excavated extensive tunnels, sent troops out secretly, set up furnaces to cast iron, and poured it upon the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He also dug tunnels ten paces inside the wall down to the water table, sent troops out through them in secret, set up furnaces to cast molten iron, and poured it on the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊遂相告曰：「不畏利槊堅城，唯畏楊公鐵星。

translations.literal: The bandits then told one another, "We do not fear sharp spears or stout walls — we only fear Lord Yang's iron stars."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then told one another, "We do not fear sharp spears or stout walls — we only fear Lord Yang's molten iron."

sentences.zh: 」津與賊帥元洪業等書喻之，並授鐵券，許之爵位，令圖賊帥毛普賢。

translations.literal: Jin wrote letters of persuasion to the bandit chiefs Yuan Hongye and others, also granted them iron certificates, promised them noble ranks, and ordered them to plot against the bandit chief Mao Puxian.
translations.idiomatic: Jin wrote to the rebel leaders Yuan Hongye and others to win them over, granted them iron certificates of mercy, promised them noble ranks, and urged them to turn against the rebel leader Mao Puxian.

sentences.zh: 洪業等感寤，復書雲欲殺普賢。

translations.literal: Hongye and the others were moved to awakening and replied by letter saying they wished to kill Puxian.
translations.idiomatic: Hongye and the others were moved by his appeal and wrote back saying they would kill Puxian.

sentences.zh: 又云：「賊欲圍城，正為取北人，城中所有人，必須盡殺。

translations.literal: They also wrote, "The bandits wish to besiege the city precisely in order to seize the northerners; everyone in the city must be killed to the last."
translations.idiomatic: They also wrote, "The rebels mean to besiege the city only to seize the northerners within it — every one of them must be killed."

sentences.zh: 」津以城內北人，雖是惡黨，然掌握中物，未忍便殺，但收內子城，防禁而已。

translations.literal: Jin, considering that the northerners within the city, though a wicked faction, yet held goods in their grasp, could not bear to kill them outright; he only gathered them into the inner citadel and placed them under guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jin could not bring himself to slaughter the northerners in the city, wicked though many of them were, since they still held property there. He only confined them to the inner citadel under guard.

sentences.zh: 將吏無不感其仁恕。

translations.literal: The generals and officials were all moved by his benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and officials were all moved by his humanity and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 朝廷初送鐵券二十枚，委津分給。

translations.literal: The court at first sent twenty iron certificates and entrusted Jin to distribute them.
translations.idiomatic: The court initially sent twenty iron certificates of mercy and entrusted Jin to distribute them.

sentences.zh: 津隨賊中首領，間行送之；

translations.literal: Jin, according to the rebel leaders, sent them by secret routes;
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent them by secret routes to the rebel leaders;

sentences.zh: 修禮、普賢頗亦由此而死。

translations.literal: Xiuli and Puxian also largely died because of this.
translations.idiomatic: and Xiuli and Puxian were largely killed as a result.

sentences.zh: 既而杜洛周圍州城，津盡力捍守。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Du Luozhou besieged the provincial city, and Jin exhausted his strength in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Du Luozhou besieged the provincial city, and Jin defended it with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 詔加衛將軍，將士有功者任津科賞，兵人給復八年。

translations.literal: An edict added the rank of General of the Guard; officers and soldiers with merit were left to Jin to reward according to merit, and common soldiers were granted eight years' tax exemption.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added the rank of General of the Guard, authorized Jin to reward meritorious officers and soldiers as he saw fit, and granted common soldiers eight years' tax exemption.

sentences.zh: 葛榮以司徒說津。

translations.literal: Ge Rong tried to persuade Jin with the offer of Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong tried to win Jin over with the offer of Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 津大怒，斬其使以絕之。

translations.literal: Jin was greatly enraged, beheaded the envoy, and broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was furious, beheaded the envoy, and broke off all contact.

sentences.zh: 自受攻圍，經歷三稔，朝廷不能拯赴。

translations.literal: From the time he came under siege, three full years passed, and the court could not come to his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the siege began three full years passed, and the court could not come to his relief.

sentences.zh: 乃遣長子遁突圍出。

translations.literal: He then sent his eldest son Dun to break through the encirclement and get out.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his eldest son Dun to break through the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 詣蠕蠕主阿那瑰，令其討賊。

translations.literal: Dun went to the Rouran ruler Anagui and asked him to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Dun went to the Rouran ruler Anagui and asked him to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 遁日夜泣訴，阿那瑰遣其從祖吐豆發率精騎南出。

translations.literal: Dun wept and pleaded day and night; Anagui sent his father's younger cousin Tudufa leading elite horsemen south.
translations.idiomatic: Dun wept and pleaded day and night, and Anagui sent his father's younger cousin Tudufa south at the head of elite cavalry.

sentences.zh: 前鋒已達廣昌，賊防塞益口，蠕蠕遂還。

translations.literal: The vanguard had already reached Guangchang, but the bandits blocked Yikou, and the Rouran therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard had already reached Guangchang, but the rebels blocked Yikou, and the Rouran withdrew.

sentences.zh: 津長史李裔引賊入，津苦戰不敵，遂見拘執。

translations.literal: Jin's chief clerk Li Yi led the bandits in; Jin fought bitterly but could not prevail, and was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's chief clerk Li Yi let the rebels in. Jin fought bitterly but could not hold, and was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 洛周脫津衣服，置地牢下數日，將烹之。

translations.literal: Luozhou stripped Jin of his clothes, placed him in a dungeon for several days, and was about to boil him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou stripped Jin of his clothes, threw him into a dungeon for several days, and was about to boil him alive.

sentences.zh: 諸賊還相諫止，遂得免害。

translations.literal: The bandits in turn admonished one another and stopped it, and so he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels admonished one another and stopped it, and he escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 津曾與裔相見，對諸賊帥以大義責之，辭淚俱發，裔大慚。

translations.literal: Jin once met Yi face to face; before the bandit chiefs he rebuked him on grounds of righteousness, words and tears issuing together, and Yi was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin once confronted Yi before the rebel chiefs and rebuked him on grounds of loyalty and duty, his words mingled with tears; Yi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 典守者以告洛周，弗之責。

translations.literal: The custodian reported this to Luozhou, who did not blame him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The jailer reported this to Luozhou, who did not punish Jin for it.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮並洛周，復為榮所拘。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong absorbed Luozhou, Jin was again held captive by Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong absorbed Luozhou's forces, Jin was again held captive by Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮破，始得還洛。

translations.literal: When Rong was defeated, Jin was at last able to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong was defeated, Jin was at last able to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an, he concurrently served as Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an he also served as Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 元顥內逼，莊帝將親出討，以津為中軍大都督，兼領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao pressed inward; Emperor Zhuang was about to go out in person to suppress him, and made Jin Grand Area Commander of the Central Army and concurrently General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao pressed inward, Emperor Zhuang prepared to lead the campaign in person and appointed Jin Grand Area Commander of the Central Army while also making him General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 未行，顥入。

translations.literal: Before he set out, Hao entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor could set out, Hao entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 及顥敗，津乃入宿殿中，掃灑宮掖，遣第二子逸封閉府庫，各令防守。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Jin entered and lodged in the palace hall, swept and cleaned the inner quarters, sent his second son Yi to seal the treasuries, and ordered each to stand guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, Jin took up residence in the palace, swept and cleaned the inner quarters, sent his second son Yi to seal the treasuries, and posted guards at each.

sentences.zh: 及帝入也，津迎於北芒，流涕謝罪。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered, Jin met him at Beimang, weeping and begging forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, Jin met him at Beimang in tears, begging forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉慰之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warmly praised and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 尋以津為司空，加侍中。

translations.literal: Soon Jin was made Minister of Works and given the additional rank of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was soon appointed Minister of Works with the additional rank of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死，使津以本官為兼尚書令、北道大行台、都督、并州刺史，委以討胡經略。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Jin was ordered to retain his present office while also serving as Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Northern Route Grand Mobile Headquarters, Area Commander, and Regional Inspector of Bing Province, entrusted with the strategy for suppressing the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong's death, Jin was ordered to retain his present office while also serving as Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, head of the Northern Route Grand Mobile Headquarters, area commander, and Regional Inspector of Bing Province, entrusted with the campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 津馳至鄴，將從滏口而入。

translations.literal: Jin galloped to Ye and was about to enter by the Fu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Jin galloped to Ye and planned to enter through the Fu Pass.

sentences.zh: 遇爾硃兆等已克洛，相州刺史李神等議欲與津舉城通款，津不從。

translations.literal: He encountered Erzhu Zhao and others, who had already taken Luoyang; Regional Inspector of Xiang Province Li Shen and others discussed surrendering the city to Jin and opening negotiations, but Jin would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He found that Erzhu Zhao and others had already taken Luoyang. Regional Inspector of Xiang Province Li Shen and others proposed surrendering the city to Jin and opening negotiations, but Jin refused.

sentences.zh: 以子逸既為光州刺史，兄子昱時為東道行台，鳩率部曲，在於梁、沛，津規欲東轉，更為方略。

translations.literal: Since his son Yi was already Regional Inspector of Guang Province and his elder brother's son Yu was then head of the Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters, each gathering troops in Liang and Pei, Jin planned to turn east and devise a new strategy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi was already Regional Inspector of Guang Province, and his elder brother's son Yu then headed the Eastern Route Mobile Headquarters, each gathering troops in Liang and Pei. Jin planned to turn east and devise a new strategy.

sentences.zh: 乃率輕騎望於濟州度河。

translations.literal: He then led light cavalry toward crossing the river at Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then led light cavalry toward Jizhou to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 而爾硃仲遠已陷東郡，所圖不果，遂還京師。

translations.literal: But Erzhu Zhongyuan had already taken Dong Commandery; the plan did not succeed, and he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: But Erzhu Zhongyuan had already taken Dong Commandery, his plan failed, and he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 普泰元年，亦遇害於洛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putai, he likewise met with violent death at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putai he was likewise killed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈大將軍，太傅、都督、雍州刺史，諡曰孝穆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously awarded General-in-Chief, Grand Tutor, Area Commander, and Regional Inspector of Yong Province, with the posthumous name Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as General-in-Chief, Grand Tutor, area commander, and Regional Inspector of Yong Province, with the posthumous name Xiaomu (Filial and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 將葬本鄉，詔大鴻臚持節監護喪事。

translations.literal: When he was to be buried in his native district, an edict ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to hold the staff of authority and supervise the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he was to be buried in his native district, an edict ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to supervise the funeral with full ceremonial authority.

sentences.zh: 長子遁。

translations.literal: His eldest son Dun.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Dun.

sentences.zh: 遁字山才。

translations.literal: Dun, style name Shancai.
translations.idiomatic: Dun, whose style name was Shancai.

sentences.zh: 其家貴顯，諸子弱冠，咸縻王爵。

translations.literal: His family was noble and eminent; when the sons reached manhood, all were awarded princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: His family was eminent and powerful, and when the sons came of age they all received princely titles.

sentences.zh: 而遁性靜退，年近三十，方為鎮西府主簿。

translations.literal: But Dun by nature was quiet and retiring; nearing thirty, he was only then made Chief Clerk of the Western Garrison Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: But Dun was quiet and retiring by nature, and not until he was nearly thirty did he become chief clerk of the Western Garrison Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左丞、金紫光祿大夫，亦被害於洛。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he rose to Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Purple-Gold Seal; he too was killed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to left assistant in the Masters of Writing and grand master of splendid happiness with purple-gold seal, and was also killed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史，諡曰恭定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously awarded General of the Cavalry and Chariots, Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Regional Inspector of You Province, with the posthumous name Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as general of the cavalry and chariots, with honors equal to the three excellencies, and inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Gongding (Respectful and Settled).

sentences.zh: 遁弟逸，字遵道，有當世才。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Yi, style name Zundao, possessed talent for his age.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Yi, styled Zundao, had talent to match his times.

sentences.zh: 起家員外散騎侍郎，以功賜爵華陰男。

translations.literal: He began his career as Supernumerary Cavaliers-in-Attendant, and for merit was ennobled as Baron of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a supernumerary cavaliers-attendant and was ennobled as Baron of Huayin for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 建義初，莊帝猶在河陽，逸獨往謁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, Emperor Zhuang was still at Heyang; Yi alone went to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era, while Emperor Zhuang was still at Heyang, Yi went alone to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 帝特除給事黃門侍郎，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: The emperor specially appointed him Gentlemen-in-Attendance of the Yellow Gate, concurrently serving as Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially appointed him gentlemen-in-attendance of the yellow gate and made him concurrent secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 及朝士濫禍，帝益憂怖，詔逸晝夜陪侍，常寢御床前。

translations.literal: When court officials suffered indiscriminate slaughter, the emperor grew ever more fearful; an edict ordered Yi to attend day and night, and he regularly slept before the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: When court officials were slaughtered indiscriminately, the emperor grew increasingly fearful. An edict ordered Yi to attend day and night, and he regularly slept beside the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 帝曾夜中謂逸曰：「昨來舉目唯見異人，賴卿差以自慰。

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Yi at night, "Yesterday when I raised my eyes I saw only strange men; thanks to you I have been somewhat consoled."
translations.idiomatic: Once at night the emperor said to Yi, "Yesterday I looked around and saw only strangers; thanks to you I find a little comfort."

sentences.zh: 」再遷南秦州刺史，加散騎常侍，時年二十九，時方伯之少，未有先之者。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Regional Inspector of Southern Qin Province, with the added rank of Regular Cavaliers-in-Attendant; he was then twenty-nine, and among provincial governors at the time, none younger had preceded him.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made inspector of Southern Qin while also appointed regular cavaliers-attendant. At twenty-nine he was the youngest regional governor anyone could remember.

sentences.zh: 仍以路阻不行，改光州刺史。

translations.literal: Because the roads were blocked he could not go; he was changed to Regional Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because the roads were blocked he could not take up the post and was reassigned as inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時災儉連歲，逸欲以倉粟振給，而所司懼罪不敢。

translations.literal: At the time famine and scarcity continued year after year; Yi wished to distribute grain from the storehouses for relief, but the responsible officials feared punishment and dared not.
translations.idiomatic: Famine had struck for years running, and Yi wanted to distribute grain from the storehouses, but the responsible officials feared punishment and dared not act.

sentences.zh: 逸曰：「國以人為本，人以食為命，假令以此獲戾，吾所甘心。

translations.literal: Yi said, "The state takes the people as its foundation, and the people take food as their life; even if I should incur blame for this, I am willing at heart."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The state is built on people, and people live by food. Even if I should be punished for this, I accept it willingly."

sentences.zh: 」遂出粟，然後申表。

translations.literal: He then released the grain, and afterward submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He released the grain and only afterward submitted a memorial reporting it.

sentences.zh: 右僕射元羅以下，謂公儲難闕，並執不許。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Yuan Luo and those below him said the public stores could hardly be diminished, and all held to their objection and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Yuan Luo and others argued that the public granaries could not be depleted, and all objected.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、臨淮王彧以為宜貸二萬，詔聽貸二萬。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masters of Writing, Prince of Linhuai Yu, thought twenty thousand should be lent; an edict permitted lending twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Linhuai Yu, thought twenty thousand should be lent; an edict authorized a loan of twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 逸既出粟之後，其老小殘疾不能自存活者，又於州門造粥飼之，將死而得濟者以萬數。

translations.literal: After Yi had released the grain, for those old, young, disabled, and unable to support themselves, he also made gruel at the provincial gate to feed them; those on the verge of death who were saved numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After releasing the grain, he set up gruel kitchens at the provincial gate for the old, young, disabled, and destitute. Tens of thousands who had been at death's door were saved.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it and praised him.

sentences.zh: 逸為政愛人，尤憎豪猾，廣設耳目，善惡畢聞。

translations.literal: In governing, Yi loved the people, especially hated the powerful and the cunning, and widely set informants so that good and evil were all heard.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yi cared for the people, hated the powerful and dishonest, and maintained a wide network of informants so that he heard of every deed, good or ill.

sentences.zh: 其兵出使下邑，皆自持糧，人或為設食者，雖在暗室，終不敢進，咸言楊使君有千里眼，那可欺之。

translations.literal: When his soldiers went on missions to subordinate districts, all carried their own provisions; though someone might prepare food for them, even in a dark room they would not dare partake in the end, all saying Intendant Yang has eyes that see a thousand leagues — how could one deceive him?
translations.idiomatic: When his soldiers went on missions to subordinate districts they carried their own provisions. Even if someone offered them food in private, they would not dare accept it, saying Intendant Yang had eyes everywhere and could not be fooled.

sentences.zh: 在州政績尤美。

translations.literal: His governance in the province was especially fine.
translations.idiomatic: His record in the province was especially distinguished.

sentences.zh: 及其家禍，爾硃仲遠遣使於州害之。

translations.literal: When the disaster befell his family, Erzhu Zhongyuan sent an envoy to the province to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck his family, Erzhu Zhongyuan sent men to the province and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 吏人如喪親戚，城邑村落營齋供，一月之中，所在不絕。

translations.literal: Officials and people mourned as if for kin; in cities, towns, and villages they set up vegetarian offerings, and within a month they never ceased wherever one went.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners mourned him as if he were kin. In towns and villages people set up memorial offerings, and for a full month such observances never ceased.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈都督、豫郢二州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously awarded Area Commander and Regional Inspector of the two provinces of Yu and Ying, with the posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as area commander and inspector of Yu and Ying provinces, with the posthumous name Zhen (Upright).

sentences.zh: 逸弟謐，字遵和。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Mi, style name Zunhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Mi, styled Zunhe.

sentences.zh: 曆員外散騎常侍，以功賜爵恆農伯，鎮軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫、衛將軍。

translations.literal: He passed through Supernumerary Regular Cavaliers-in-Attendant; for merit was ennobled Baron of Hengnong, General Who Stabilizes the Army, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Purple-Gold Seal, and General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He served as supernumerary regular cavaliers-attendant and was ennobled Baron of Hengnong for merit, rising to general who stabilizes the army, grand master of splendid happiness with purple-gold seal, and general of the guard.

sentences.zh: 在晉陽，為爾硃兆所害。

translations.literal: While at Jinyang, he was killed by Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: While at Jinyang he was killed by Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，贈驃騎將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was posthumously awarded General of Agile Cavalry and Regional Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taichang era he was posthumously honored as general of agile cavalry and inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 謐弟愔，事列於後。

translations.literal: Mi's younger brother Yin — his account is given below.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's younger brother Yin is treated below.

sentences.zh: 津弟痈，字延季。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Yong, style name Yanji.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Yong, styled Yanji.

sentences.zh: 弘厚，頗有文學。

translations.literal: He was magnanimous and generous, and possessed considerable literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was broad-minded and accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 位武衛將軍，加散騎常侍、安南將軍。

translations.literal: He attained the rank of General of the Martial Guard, with the added ranks of Regular Cavaliers-in-Attendant and General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the martial guard, with the added ranks of regular cavaliers-attendant and general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，遇害河陰，曾儀同三司、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang, he met his end at Heyin; he had once held Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies and been Regional Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin. He had previously held honors equal to the three excellencies and served as inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 播家世純厚，為並敦議讓，昆季相事，有如父子。

translations.literal: The Bo family's generations were pure and generous, all together earnest in courtesy and yielding; the brothers served one another as if father and son.
translations.idiomatic: The Bo family was known for pure-hearted generations, mutual courtesy, and brothers who served one another as faithfully as fathers and sons.

sentences.zh: 播性剛毅，椿、津恭謙，兄弟旦則聚於査堂，終日相對，未曾入內。

translations.literal: Bo was firm and resolute by nature; Chun and Jin were respectful and modest — the brothers gathered in the hall by day, facing one another all day, never going inside.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was firm by nature, while Chun and Jin were respectful and modest. The brothers spent their days together in the hall, face to face, never withdrawing indoors.

sentences.zh: 有一美味，不集不食。

translations.literal: When there was one fine delicacy, if the gathering was not complete they would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: They would not taste a fine dish unless all were assembled.

sentences.zh: 査堂間，往往幃慢隔障，為寢息之所，時就休偃，還共談笑。

translations.literal: Between the halls there were often curtains and screens as partitions forming places for rest; they would go there to lie down for a while, then return to talk and laugh together.
translations.idiomatic: Curtains and screens between the halls formed resting places where they would nap and then return to talk and laugh together.

sentences.zh: 椿年老，曾他處醉歸，津扶侍還室，仍假寢閣前，承候安否。

translations.literal: When Chun grew old, once when he returned drunk from elsewhere, Jin supported him back to his room, then lay down to sleep before the gate pavilion to await word of whether he was safe.
translations.idiomatic: When Chun was old, Jin once helped him home after he returned drunk from elsewhere, then slept outside his door to be on hand if needed.

sentences.zh: 椿、津年過六十，並登臺鼎；

translations.literal: Chun and Jin, both past sixty, both ascended to the highest offices;
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Jin, both past sixty, both reached the highest offices;

sentences.zh: 而津常旦暮參問，子侄羅列階下，椿不命坐，津不敢坐。

translations.literal: Yet Jin regularly attended morning and evening to inquire after him; nephews lined the steps below; Chun did not command him to sit, and Jin dared not sit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin still attended Chun morning and evening. When nephews filled the steps below, Chun would not tell Jin to sit, and Jin would not dare sit.

sentences.zh: 椿每近出，或日斜不至，津不先飯；

translations.literal: Whenever Chun went out on a short trip, if he failed to return even at sunset Jin would not eat first;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chun went out for the day, if he had not returned by sunset Jin would not eat first;

sentences.zh: 椿還，然後共食。

translations.literal: When Chun returned, then they would eat together.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Chun returned would they eat together.

sentences.zh: 食則津親授匙箸，味皆先嘗，椿命食，然後食。

translations.literal: At meals Jin personally handed spoon and chopsticks; he tasted every dish first; when Chun commanded eating, then he ate.
translations.idiomatic: At meals Jin personally handed his brother spoon and chopsticks, tasted every dish first, and ate only when Chun told him to.

sentences.zh: 津為司空，于時府主皆自引寮佐。

translations.literal: When Jin was Minister of Works, at that time heads of offices all themselves introduced their staff members.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was Minister of Works, department heads normally introduced their own staff for appointments.

sentences.zh: 人有就津求官者，津曰：「此事須家兄裁之，何為見問。

translations.literal: When someone came to Jin to seek an office, Jin said, "This matter must be decided by my elder brother — why ask me?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone came to Jin seeking an office, Jin said, "That is for my elder brother to decide — why ask me?"

sentences.zh: 」初，津為肆州，椿在京宅，每有四時嘉味，輒因使次附之，若或未寄，不先入口。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jin was in Si Province and Chun was at the capital residence, whenever there were seasonal delicacies he always sent them along with the next courier; if they had not yet been sent, he would not taste them first.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was in Si Province and Chun remained in the capital, he always sent seasonal delicacies with the next courier. If they had not yet been sent, he would not taste them first.

sentences.zh: 椿每得所寄，輒對之下泣。

translations.literal: Whenever Chun received what was sent, he would weep over it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chun received what Jin sent, he wept over it.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並皆有孫，唯椿有曾孫，年十五六矣。

translations.literal: All the brothers had grandsons; only Chun had a great-grandson, already fifteen or sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: All the brothers had grandsons, but only Chun had a great-grandson, already fifteen or sixteen.

sentences.zh: 椿常欲為之早娶，望見玄孫。

translations.literal: Chun often wished to marry him off early, hoping to see a great-great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Chun often wished to marry him off early in hopes of seeing a great-great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 自昱已下，率多學尚，時人莫不欽焉。

translations.literal: From Yu downward, most pursued learning and refinement; people of the time all admired them.
translations.idiomatic: From Yu's generation down, most pursued learning, and people of the age admired them.

sentences.zh: 一家之內，男女百口，緦服同爨，庭無間言。

translations.literal: Within one household, men and women numbered a hundred mouths; they wore mourning dress and shared one kitchen — in the courtyard there were no harsh words.
translations.idiomatic: In one household a hundred men and women shared mourning dress and one kitchen, and there was never an angry word in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 魏世以來，唯有盧陽烏兄弟及播昆季，當世莫逮焉。

translations.literal: Since the Wei, only the brothers Lu Yangwu and the Bo brothers could compare — no one of their time matched them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wei dynasty, only the brothers Lu Yangwu and the Bo brothers had rivaled them — no family of their age could match them.

sentences.zh: 爾硃世隆等將害椿家，誣其為逆，奏請收之。

translations.literal: Erzhu Shilong and others were about to harm the Chun family, falsely accused them of rebellion, and memorialized requesting their arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong and others planned to destroy Chun's family, falsely accused them of rebellion, and memorialized requesting their arrest.

sentences.zh: 節閔不許；

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin did not agree;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiemin refused;

sentences.zh: 世隆復苦執，不得已，乃下詔。

translations.literal: Shilong again pressed stubbornly, and unable to refuse, the emperor issued an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong pressed again, and the emperor reluctantly issued an edict.

sentences.zh: 世隆遂遣步騎夜圍其宅，天光亦同日收椿于華陰，東西兩處，無少長皆遇禍，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Shilong then sent infantry and cavalry by night to surround their residence; Tianguang also on the same day seized Chun at Huayin — east and west, in both places, none young or old escaped disaster; their property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong sent foot and horse soldiers by night to surround their residence, and Tianguang on the same day seized Chun at Huayin. In both places, young and old alike perished, and their property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 節閔惋悵久之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jiemin grieved and lamented for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiemin grieved over it for a long time.

sentences.zh: 愔字遵彥，小名秦王。

translations.literal: Yin, style name Zunyan, nickname Qinwang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, styled Zunyan, bore the childhood name Qinwang.

sentences.zh: 兒童時，口若不能言；

translations.literal: In childhood he seemed as though he could not speak;
translations.idiomatic: As a child he seemed barely able to speak;

sentences.zh: 而風度深敏，出入門閭，未嘗戲弄。

translations.literal: Yet his bearing was deeply acute; going in and out of lanes and alleys, he never played or frolicked.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his bearing was deeply perceptive, and he never frolicked in the streets.

sentences.zh: 六歲學史書，十一受《詩》、《易》，好《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: At six he studied the histories; at eleven he received instruction in the Book of Songs and the Book of Changes; he loved the Zuo Tradition on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: At six he studied history; at eleven he began the Book of Songs and the Book of Changes; he loved the Zuo Tradition on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 幼喪母，曾詣舅源子恭。

translations.literal: He lost his mother young; once he went to visit his maternal uncle Yuan Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother young and once visited his maternal uncle Yuan Zigong.

sentences.zh: 子恭與之飲，問讀何書。

translations.literal: Zigong drank with him and asked what book he was reading.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong drank with him and asked what book he was studying.

translations.literal: He said, "Reciting the Book of Songs."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Reciting the Book of Songs."

sentences.zh: 子恭曰：「誦至《渭陽》未邪？

translations.literal: Zigong said, "Have you reached 'Wei Yang' yet?"
translations.idiomatic: Zigong asked, "Have you reached 'Wei Yang' yet?"

sentences.zh: 」愔便號泣感噎。

translations.literal: Yin immediately wailed and wept from choking emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yin immediately burst into sobs, choked with grief.

sentences.zh: 子恭亦對之歔欷，遂為之罷酒。

translations.literal: Zigong also sighed in grief facing him, and thereupon stopped the drinking for his sake.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong sighed in response and stopped the drinking party.

sentences.zh: 子恭後謂津曰：「常謂秦王不甚察慧，從今已後，更欲刮目視之。」

translations.literal: Later Zigong said to Jin, "I always said Qinwang was not very perceptive and bright; from now on I shall look at him with fresh eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Later Zigong told Jin, "I always thought Qinwang was not very bright. From now on I shall look at him with fresh eyes."

sentences.zh: 愔一門四世同居，家甚隆盛，昆季就學者三十餘人。

translations.literal: Yin's clan lived together four generations in one household; the family was very prosperous; more than thirty brothers and cousins attended school.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's clan lived together for four generations; the household was prosperous, and more than thirty brothers and cousins attended school together.

sentences.zh: 學庭前有柰樹，實落地，群兒咸爭之。

translations.literal: Before the school courtyard there was a nashi tree; when the fruit fell to the ground, all the children scrambled for it.
translations.idiomatic: A nashi tree stood before the school courtyard, and when the fruit fell to the ground all the children scrambled for it.

sentences.zh: 愔頹然獨坐。

translations.literal: Yin sat alone with relaxed detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sat apart, unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 其季父痈適入學館，見之，大用嗟異。

translations.literal: His younger uncle Yong happened to enter the academy and, seeing this, greatly admired it in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yong happened into the academy and was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 顧謂賓客曰：「此兒恬裕，有我家風。

translations.literal: He turned and said to the guests, "This boy is calm and generous — he has our family's style."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his guests he said, "This boy is calm and generous — he has our family character."

sentences.zh: 」宅內有茂竹，遂為愔于林邊別葺一室，命獨處其中，常銅盤具盛饌以飯之。

translations.literal: Within the residence there was dense bamboo; he then had a separate room built for Yin beside the grove, ordered him to live alone within it, and regularly set out a bronze platter with lavish fare to feed him.
translations.idiomatic: The estate had a grove of bamboo, and Yong had a separate room built for Yin beside it, where he was to live alone. Yong regularly sent him a bronze platter of fine food.

sentences.zh: 因以督厲諸子曰：「汝輩但如遵彥謹慎，自得竹林別室、銅盤重肉之食。

translations.literal: Thereby he urged and encouraged the other sons, saying, "You need only be as careful as Zunyan, and you too will get a separate bamboo-grove chamber and bronze-platter feasts of heavy meat."
translations.idiomatic: He used this to exhort the other boys: "If you are as careful as Zunyan, you too will earn a private room beside the bamboo grove and meals on a bronze platter laden with meat."

sentences.zh: 」愔從父兄黃門侍郎昱特相器重，曾謂人曰：「此兒駒齒未落，已是我家龍文；

translations.literal: Yin's elder cousin Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate Yu especially valued him; he once told someone, "This boy's colt teeth have not yet fallen — already he is the dragon pattern of our house."
translations.idiomatic: Yin's elder cousin Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu especially valued him and once said, "This boy still has his milk teeth, yet he is already the dragon of our house."

sentences.zh: 更十歲後，當求之千里外。

translations.literal: Ten years hence, one will seek his like a thousand leagues away.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years from now people will seek his like from a thousand leagues away.

sentences.zh: 」昱嘗與十餘人賦詩，愔一覽便誦，無所遺失。

translations.literal: Yu once composed poems with more than ten people; Yin read them once and then recited them, missing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu once composed poems with a dozen others; Yin read them once and recited them without omitting a word.

sentences.zh: 及長，能清言，美音制，風神俊悟，容止可觀，人士見之，莫不敬異；

translations.literal: When grown, he could discourse in pure conversation, had a beautiful voice, a spirit that was sharp and bright, deportment worthy of regard; scholars and gentlemen who saw him all respected and marveled;
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he excelled at pure talk, had a fine voice, a sharp and radiant presence, and dignified bearing. Scholars who met him all regarded him with awe;

sentences.zh: 有識者多以遠大許之。

translations.literal: Those with insight mostly promised him a far-reaching future.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment all foretold a great future for him.

sentences.zh: 正光中，隨父之并州。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he followed his father to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era he accompanied his father to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 性既恬默，又好山水，遂入晉陽西縣甕山讀書。

translations.literal: His nature being quiet and withdrawn, and also loving mountains and waters, he entered Weng Mountain in Xixian of Jinyang to study.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet by nature and fond of landscape, he went to Weng Mountain in Xixian near Jinyang to study.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，津為定州刺史，愔亦隨父之職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Jin was Regional Inspector of Ding Province, and Yin also followed his father to his post.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xiaochang era Jin became inspector of Dingzhou, and Yin accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 以軍功除羽林監，賜爵魏昌男，不拜。

translations.literal: For military merit he was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard and ennobled Baron of Weichang; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was appointed supervisor of the feathered forest guard and ennobled Baron of Weichang, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 及中山為杜洛周陷，全家被囚縶。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was taken by Du Luozhou, the whole family was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongshan fell to Du Luozhou, the entire family was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 未幾，洛周滅，又沒葛榮。

translations.literal: Before long Luozhou was destroyed, and they fell into Ge Rong's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Luozhou was defeated and they fell into Ge Rong's hands.

sentences.zh: 榮欲以女妻之，又逼以偽職。

translations.literal: Rong wished to give him his daughter in marriage and also forced a false office upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to marry his daughter to Yin and also pressed a bogus office on him.

sentences.zh: 愔乃托疾，密含牛血數合，於眾中吐之，仍陽喑不語。

translations.literal: Yin then feigned illness, secretly held several he of ox blood in his mouth, spewed it before the crowd, and still pretended to be mute and not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yin feigned illness, secretly held several he of ox blood in his mouth, vomited it before the crowd, and then played deaf and mute.

sentences.zh: 榮以為信然，乃止。

translations.literal: Rong believed it was real and therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Rong believed him and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 永安初，還洛，拜通直散騎侍郎，年十八。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongan, he returned to Luoyang and was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier; he was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yongan era he returned to Luoyang and was appointed attendant cavalier for direct counsel at eighteen.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛時，愔從父兄侃為北中郎將，鎮河梁。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yin's elder cousin Kan was General of the Northern Gentlemen and garrisoned Heliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yin's elder cousin Kan was general of the northern gentlemen, stationed at Heliang.

sentences.zh: 愔適至侃處，便屬乘輿失守，夜至河。

translations.literal: Yin happened to arrive at Kan's place just when the imperial carriage lost its position and came by night to the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yin happened to reach Kan just as the emperor lost control of the capital and fled by night to the river.

sentences.zh: 侃雖奉迎車駕北度，而潛南奔。

translations.literal: Although Kan outwardly escorted the imperial carriage north across the river, secretly he fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Although Kan outwardly escorted the imperial carriage north across the river, he secretly planned to flee south.

sentences.zh: 愔固諫止之，遂相與扈從達建州。

translations.literal: Yin firmly remonstrated and stopped him; they then together escorted the emperor and reached Jian Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yin firmly remonstrated and stopped him, and together they escorted the emperor to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant Cavalier for Direct Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regular attendant cavalier for direct counsel.

sentences.zh: 愔以世故未夷，志在潛退，乃謝病。

translations.literal: Yin, because the times were not yet settled, set his mind on retiring in secret, and thereupon pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: Believing the times were still unsettled, Yin wished to withdraw quietly and pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 與友人中直侍郎河間邢邵隱於嵩山。

translations.literal: With his friend Attendant-in-Ordinary for Direct Service Xing Shao of Hejian, he went into seclusion on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: With his friend Attendant-in-Ordinary Xing Shao of Hejian he went into seclusion on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝誅爾硃榮，其從兄侃參贊帷幄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, his elder cousin Kan assisted in the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang executed Erzhu Rong, his elder cousin Kan served as an adviser in the command tent.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其父津為并州刺史、北道大行台，愔隨之任。

translations.literal: The court appointed his father Jin Regional Inspector of Bing Province and Northern Route Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Yin followed him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed his father Jin inspector of Bingzhou and head of the Northern Route Grand Mobile Headquarters, and Yin accompanied him to his post.

sentences.zh: 有邯鄲人楊寬者，求義從出籓，愔請津納之。

translations.literal: There was one Yang Kuan of Handan who sought to follow them righteously out of the province; Yin asked Jin to take him in.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Handan named Yang Kuan asked to follow them out of the province in loyal service, and Yin persuaded Jin to accept him.

sentences.zh: 俄而孝莊幽崩，愔時適欲還都，行達邯鄲，過楊寬家，為寬所執。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Xiaozhuang died under confinement; Yin at that time was about to return to the capital, reached Handan on the road, passed Yang Kuan's house, and was seized by Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Xiaozhuang died in confinement. Yin was then on his way back to the capital; when he reached Handan and passed Yang Kuan's house, Kuan seized him.

sentences.zh: 至相州，見刺史劉誕，以愔名家盛德，甚相哀念，付長史慕容白澤禁止焉。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiang Province and met Regional Inspector Liu Yan, because Yin was of a famous clan and eminent virtue, Yan greatly pitied him and entrusted him to Chief Clerk Murong Baize for confinement.
