translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xiangzhou he met Regional Inspector Liu Yan, who pitied Yin as a man of famous lineage and high character and entrusted him to chief clerk Murong Baize for confinement.

sentences.zh: 遣隊主鞏榮貴防禁送都，至安陽亭，愔謂榮貴曰：「僕百世忠臣，輸誠魏室，家亡國破，一至於此。

translations.literal: A team commander Gong Ronggui was sent to guard him and escort him to the capital; at Anyang Pavilion, Yin said to Ronggui, "I am a loyal subject of a hundred generations who devoted his heart to the Wei house; my family is ruined and the state broken — it has come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Team commander Gong Ronggui was sent to guard and escort him to the capital. At Anyang Pavilion Yin said to Ronggui, "My family has served as loyal subjects for generations and gave our hearts to Wei. Now my family is destroyed and the state is broken — and it has come to this."

sentences.zh: 雖曰囚虜，復何面目見君父之讎！

translations.literal: Though called a captive, how could I have the face to see my lord and father's enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Though I am called a prisoner, how could I face my sovereign's murderers!

sentences.zh: 得自縊於一繩，傳首而去，君之惠也。

translations.literal: If I could hang myself with one cord and you carry off my head, that would be your kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Let me hang myself, and you carry off my head — that would be a kindness from you.

sentences.zh: 」榮貴深相矜感，遂與俱逃。

translations.literal: Ronggui was deeply moved with pity and sympathy, and fled together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved, Ronggui fled with him.

sentences.zh: 愔乃投高昂兄弟。

translations.literal: Yin then went to seek refuge with Gao Ang and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then fled to Gao Ang and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 既潛竄累載，屬齊神武至信都，遂投刺轅門。

translations.literal: Having hidden in flight for several years, when Qi Shenwu arrived at Xindu, he then submitted a calling card at the headquarters gate.
translations.idiomatic: After years in hiding, when Northern Qi founder Gao Huan reached Xindu, Yin presented his calling card at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 便蒙引見，讚揚興運，陳訴家禍，言辭哀壯，涕泗橫集。

translations.literal: He was granted an audience, praised the rising fortune, recounted his family's calamity, his words sorrowful and impassioned, tears streaming in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan received him at once, heard him praise the rising fortune and recount his family's ruin, and was moved by his grief-stricken, impassioned words and streaming tears.

sentences.zh: 神武為之改容，即署行台郎中。

translations.literal: Shenwu changed expression on his account and immediately appointed him Gentleman of the Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan's expression softened, and he immediately appointed Yin gentleman of the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 南攻鄴，曆楊寬村，寬于馬前叩頭請罪。

translations.literal: Advancing south to attack Ye, he passed through Yang Kuan's village; Kuan kowtowed before his horse begging forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern campaign against Ye they passed through Yang Kuan's village, and Kuan kowtowed before Yin's horse to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 愔謂曰：「人不識恩義，蓋亦常理。

translations.literal: Yin said to him, "That a man fails to recognize gratitude and duty is after all the ordinary way of things."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "It is only human to fail to recognize gratitude and loyalty."

sentences.zh: 我不恨卿，無假驚怖。

translations.literal: I do not hate you — do not need to be so frightened.
translations.idiomatic: I bear you no grudge, so have no need to fear.

sentences.zh: 」時鄴未下，神武命愔作祭天文，燎畢而城陷。

translations.literal: At that time Ye had not yet fallen; Shenwu ordered Yin to compose a prayer to Heaven; when the burning was finished the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had not yet fallen, and Gao Huan ordered Yin to compose an address to Heaven. When the rite was complete the city fell.

sentences.zh: 由是轉大行台右丞。

translations.literal: Because of this he was transferred to Right Assistant of the Grand Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made right assistant of the grand mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 于時霸圖草創，軍國務廣，文檄教令皆自愔及崔甗出。

translations.literal: At that time the hegemonic design was newly established and military and state affairs were broad; proclamations and edicts all issued from Yin and Cui Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the new regime was being established and military and civil business was vast; proclamations and edicts issued from Yin and Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 遭罹家難，常以喪禮自居，所食唯鹽米而已，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: Having suffered family disaster, he constantly conducted himself according to mourning rites; what he ate was only salt and rice; grief wore him to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Stricken by family disaster, he lived as if in mourning, eating only salt and rice until grief wore him to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 神武湣之，常相開慰。

translations.literal: Shenwu pitied him and often consoled and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan pitied him and often comforted him.

sentences.zh: 及韓陵之戰，愔每陣先登。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hanling, Yin in every engagement was first to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Hanling Yin led every charge.

sentences.zh: 朋僚咸共怪歎曰：「楊氏儒生，今遂為武士，仁者必勇，定非虛論。

translations.literal: Colleagues all marveled and exclaimed, "The Confucian of the Yang clan has now become a warrior — the benevolent must be brave; this is no empty saying."
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues marveled and said, "The Yang clan's scholar has become a warrior — the benevolent must be brave; that is no empty saying."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，表請解職還葬，一門之內，贈太師、太傅、丞相、大將軍者二人；

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized requesting leave from office to return for burial; within one clan, two were posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Chancellor, and General-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he memorialized requesting leave to return for burial. Within the clan alone, two men were posthumously honored as grand preceptor, grand tutor, chancellor, and general-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 太尉、錄尚書及尚書令者三人；

translations.literal: Grand Guardian, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Minister over the Masters of Writing — three men;
translations.idiomatic: grand guardian, supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and minister over the Masters of Writing — three men;

sentences.zh: 僕射、尚書者五人；

translations.literal: Vice Director and Ministers of the Masters of Writing — five men;
translations.idiomatic: vice directors and ministers of the Masters of Writing — five men;

sentences.zh: 刺史、太守者二十餘人。

translations.literal: Regional Inspectors and Grand Administrators — more than twenty men.
translations.idiomatic: regional inspectors and grand administrators — more than twenty men.

sentences.zh: 追榮之盛，古今未之有也。

translations.literal: The splendor of posthumous honors was unmatched in ancient or modern times.
translations.idiomatic: The scale of posthumous honors was unmatched in history.

sentences.zh: 及喪柩進發，吉凶儀衛亙二十餘里，會葬者將萬人。

translations.literal: When the coffin set out, the auspicious and inauspicious ceremonial escort extended more than twenty li, and those attending the burial numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin set out, the funeral procession stretched more than twenty li, and nearly ten thousand people attended the burial.

sentences.zh: 是日，隆冬盛寒，風雪嚴厚，愔跣步號哭，見者無不哀之。

translations.literal: That day, in deep midwinter with fierce cold, wind and snow heavy and thick, Yin walked barefoot weeping and wailing; all who saw him were moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: That day, in deep winter with fierce wind and snow, Yin walked barefoot weeping. All who saw him were moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 尋征赴晉陽，仍居本職。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was summoned to Jinyang and again held his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to Jinyang and resumed his former office.

sentences.zh: 愔從兄幼卿為岐州刺史，以直言忤旨見誅。

translations.literal: Yin's elder cousin Youqing was Regional Inspector of Qi Province and was executed for speaking bluntly against the emperor's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's elder cousin Youqing, regional inspector of Qizhou, was executed for speaking bluntly against the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 愔聞之悲懼，因哀感發疾，後取急就雁門溫湯療疾。

translations.literal: When Yin heard this he was grieved and fearful; grief and alarm brought on illness, and he later took emergency leave to go to the hot springs at Yanmen to treat his illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin heard this he was stricken with grief and fear, fell ill, and later took emergency leave to treat himself at the hot springs of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 郭季素害其能，因致書恐之曰：「高王欲送卿於帝所。

translations.literal: Guo Jisu, who envied his ability, therefore sent a letter threatening him, saying, "Lord Gao wishes to send you to the emperor's court."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jisu, who envied his talent, sent a threatening letter saying, "Lord Gao wishes to send you to the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」仍勸其逃亡。

translations.literal: He also urged him to flee.
translations.idiomatic: He also advised him to flee.

sentences.zh: 愔遂棄衣冠于水濱，若見沈者。

translations.literal: Yin then cast off his hat and robes at the water's edge as if he had drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Yin cast his hat and robes into the river as if he had drowned.

sentences.zh: 變易名姓，自稱劉士安。

translations.literal: He changed his name and called himself Liu Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his name and surname, calling himself Liu Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 入嵩山，與沙門曇謨征等屏居削跡。

translations.literal: He entered Mount Song and lived in seclusion with the monk Tanmozheng and others, erasing all traces.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Mount Song and lived in seclusion with the monk Tanmozheng and others, erasing all traces of himself.

sentences.zh: 又潛之光州，因東入田橫島，以講誦為業，海隅之士謂之劉先生。

translations.literal: He also went secretly to Guang Province, then entered Tianheng Island to the east, making lecturing and recitation his livelihood; scholars of the coast called him Master Liu.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly went to Guangzhou, then east to Tianheng Island, where he made a living by lecturing and recitation. Coastal scholars called him Master Liu.

sentences.zh: 太守王元景陰佑之。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Wang Yuanjing secretly protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Wang Yuanjing secretly sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 神武知愔存，遣愔從兄寶猗齎書慰喻；

translations.literal: When Shenwu learned Yin was alive, he sent Yin's elder cousin Baoqi with a letter of consolation and persuasion;
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan learned Yin was alive, he sent Yin's elder cousin Baoqi with a letter of reassurance;

sentences.zh: 仍遣光州刺史奚思業令搜訪，以禮發遣。

translations.literal: He also sent Regional Inspector of Guang Province Xi Siye to search for him and send him off with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent Regional Inspector of Guang Province Xi Siye to find him and escort him back with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 神武見之悅，除太原公開府司馬，轉長史，復授大行台右丞，封華陰縣侯，遷給事黃門侍郎，妻以庶女。

translations.literal: Shenwu was pleased to see him, appointed him Opening Staff Major of the Duke of Taiyuan, transferred him to Chief Clerk, again awarded him Right Assistant of the Grand Mobile Headquarters, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huayin County, promoted him to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, and gave him a concubine daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was delighted to see him, appointed him opening staff major to the Duke of Taiyuan, then chief clerk, again made him right assistant of the grand mobile headquarters, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Huayin, promoted him to attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate, and married him to a concubine daughter.

sentences.zh: 又兼散騎常侍，為聘梁使主。

translations.literal: He was also concurrently Regular Cavaliers-in-Attendant and served as chief envoy on a mission of marriage to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as regular cavaliers-attendant and headed an embassy of marriage to Liang.

sentences.zh: 至碻磝，州內有愔家舊佛寺。

translations.literal: When he reached Que'ao, within the province there was an old Buddhist temple of Yin's family.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Que'ao there was an old family Buddhist temple in the province.

sentences.zh: 精廬禮拜，見太傅容像，悲感慟哭，嘔血數升，遂發病不成行，輿疾還鄴。

translations.literal: He worshipped in the refined hall and saw the portrait of the Grand Tutor; moved to grief he wailed bitterly, vomited several sheng of blood, fell ill and could not continue the journey, and was carried back to Ye in illness.
translations.idiomatic: He worshipped in the temple hall and saw the portrait of the Grand Tutor. Overcome with grief he wailed, vomited blood, fell too ill to travel, and was carried back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 久之，以本官兼尚書吏部郎中。

translations.literal: After a long while, in his former office he was concurrently Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was concurrently made gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in his former rank.

sentences.zh: 武定末，以望實之美，超拜吏部尚書，加侍中、衛將軍，侍學典選如故。

translations.literal: Late in Wuding, because of the beauty of his reputation and substance, he was promoted over others to Minister of the Masters of Writing, with the added ranks of Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Guard, continuing to oversee learning and selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Wuding era, on the strength of his reputation he was promoted over others to minister of the Masters of Writing, with the added ranks of attendant-in-ordinary and general of the guard, while continuing to oversee learning and selection as before.

sentences.zh: 天保初，以本官領太子少傅，別封陽夏縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, in his former office he was appointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and separately enfeoffed as Baron of Yangxia County.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was appointed junior tutor of the crown prince in his former rank and separately enfeoffed as Baron of Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 又詔監太史，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered him to supervise the Grand Astrologer, and he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also made him supervisor of the grand astrologer, and he was transferred to right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尚太原長公主，即魏孝靜後也。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Taiyuan, who was the empress of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Taiyuan, who had been Empress of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei.

sentences.zh: 會有雉集其舍，又拜開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射，改封華山郡公。

translations.literal: When pheasants gathered at his residence, he was again appointed Opening General with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Huashan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When pheasants gathered at his residence, he was again appointed opening general with honors equal to the three excellencies and right vice director of the Masters of Writing, and his title was changed to Duke of Huashan.

sentences.zh: 九年，徙尚書令，又拜特進、驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Minister over the Masters of Writing, and again awarded Special Advancement and General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made minister over the Masters of Writing and again granted special advancement and general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十年，封開封王。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In his tenth year he was made Prince of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 文宣之崩，百寮莫有下淚，愔悲不自勝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan died, none of the hundred officials wept; Yin alone could not contain his grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan died, none of the hundred officials wept; Yin alone was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 濟南嗣業，任遇益隆，朝章國命，一人而已。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jinan succeeded, his appointments and favor grew ever greater; court regulations and state policy rested in him alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jinan took the throne, Yang Yin's appointments and favor grew ever greater; court regulations and state policy rested in his hands alone.

sentences.zh: 推誠體道，時無異議。

translations.literal: He gave his heart in sincerity and embodied the Way; at the time there was no dissenting opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his heart in sincerity and embodied the Way, and at the time there was no dissent.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年二月，為孝昭帝所誅，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qianming, he was executed by Emperor Xiaozhao; he was then fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Qianming he was executed by Emperor Xiaozhao at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 天統末，追贈司空公。

translations.literal: Late in Tiantong, he was posthumously awarded Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tiantong era he was posthumously honored as Duke of Works.

sentences.zh: 愔貴公子，早著聲譽，風表鑒裁，為朝野所稱。

translations.literal: Yin was a noble scion who early won reputation; his bearing and discernment were praised by court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was a noble scion who won early renown; court and countryside alike praised his bearing and discernment.

sentences.zh: 家門遇禍，唯有二弟一妹及兄孫女數人。

translations.literal: When disaster struck his family, only two younger brothers, one younger sister, and several grand-nieces of his elder brother remained.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck his family, only two younger brothers, one younger sister, and several of his elder brother's granddaughters survived.

sentences.zh: 撫養孤幼，慈旨溫顏，咸出仁厚。

translations.literal: He raised the orphaned and young with kindly intent and gentle countenance, all springing from humane generosity.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the orphaned and young with kindly intent and gentle countenance, all from humane generosity.

sentences.zh: 重分義，輕貨財，前後賜與，多散之親族。

translations.literal: He valued loyalty and duty and lightly regarded wealth; gifts and rewards before and after he mostly distributed among his kin.
translations.idiomatic: He valued loyalty and duty over wealth and distributed most of his rewards among his kin.

sentences.zh: 群從弟侄十數人，並待而舉火。

translations.literal: More than ten younger cousins and nephews all depended on him for their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten younger cousins and nephews all relied on him for their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 頻遭迍厄，冒履艱危，一飡之惠，酬答必重；

translations.literal: Repeatedly encountering adversity, he braved hardship and danger; a single meal's kindness he repaid heavily;
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly facing adversity, he braved hardship and danger; he repaid even a single meal's kindness heavily;

sentences.zh: 性命之仇，舍而不問。

translations.literal: Enemies who threatened his life he spared and did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: enemies who threatened his life he spared and did not pursue.

sentences.zh: 典選二十餘年，獎擢人倫，以為已任。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years he managed selection, promoting human talent and taking it as his own duty.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years he managed selection, promoting talent and taking it as his own duty.

sentences.zh: 然取士多以言貌，時致謗言，以為愔之用人，似貧士市瓜，取其大者。

translations.literal: Yet in choosing men he often relied on speech and appearance, which at times drew criticism that Yin's selection of men was like a poor man buying melons — taking the largest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he often chose men by speech and appearance, drawing criticism that Yin's selection was like a poor man buying melons — taking the largest.

sentences.zh: 愔聞，不以為意。

translations.literal: When Yin heard this he paid it no mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin heard of it, he paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 其聰記強識，半面不忘。

translations.literal: His intelligence and memory were strong; he forgot no face he had seen once.
translations.idiomatic: His intelligence and memory were formidable; he forgot no face he had seen once.

sentences.zh: 每有所召，或單稱姓，或單稱名，無有誤者。

translations.literal: Whenever he summoned someone, he might use surname alone or given name alone, and never made a mistake.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he summoned someone he might use surname alone or given name alone, and never made a mistake.

sentences.zh: 後有選人魯漫漢，自言猥賤，獨不見識。

translations.literal: Later a candidate Lu Manhan said of himself that he was low and base and alone had not been recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Later a candidate Lu Manhan said he was lowborn and alone had not been recognized.

sentences.zh: 愔曰：「卿前在元子思坊騎禿尾草驢，經見我不下，以方麹鄣面，我何不識卿？

translations.literal: Yin said, "You once rode a bald-tailed donkey in Yuan Zisi Lane, passed me without dismounting, and covered your face with square-leaven bread — how could I not recognize you?
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "You once rode a bald-tailed donkey in Yuan Zisi Lane, passed me without dismounting, and covered your face with square-leaven bread — how could I not recognize you?"

sentences.zh: 」漫漢驚服。

translations.literal: Manhan was startled and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Manhan was startled and submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 又調之曰：「名以定體，漫漢果自不虛。

translations.literal: He also teased him, saying, "The name fixes the substance — Manhan indeed lives up to his name."
translations.idiomatic: He also teased him, saying, "The name fixes the substance — Manhan truly lives up to his name."

sentences.zh: 」又令吏唱人名，誤以盧士深為士琛。

translations.literal: He also had an official call out names and mistakenly called Lu Shishen Shishen.
translations.idiomatic: He also had an official call out names and mistakenly called Lu Shishen by the name Shishen.

sentences.zh: 士深自言，愔曰：「盧郎潤朗，所以比玉。」

translations.literal: Shishen spoke up himself; Yin said, "Master Lu is lustrous and bright, hence the comparison to jade."
translations.idiomatic: Shishen spoke up for himself; Yin said, "Master Lu is lustrous and bright — that is why he is compared to jade."

sentences.zh: 自尚公主後，衣紫羅袍、金鏤大帶。

translations.literal: After marrying the princess he wore purple gauze robes and a gold-inlaid great belt.
translations.idiomatic: After marrying the princess he wore purple gauze robes and a great belt inlaid with gold.

sentences.zh: 遇李庶，頗以為恥，謂曰：「我此衣服，都是內裁，既見子將，不能無愧。」

translations.literal: Meeting Li Shu, he was somewhat ashamed and said, "These clothes of mine were all cut within the palace; now that I see you, Zijiang, I cannot but feel ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Li Shu, he felt somewhat ashamed and said, "These clothes of mine were all cut within the palace; now that I see you, Zijiang, I cannot but feel ashamed."

sentences.zh: 及居端揆，經綜機衡，千端萬緒，神無滯用。

translations.literal: When he occupied the chief minister's seat, he managed the pivots of state; amid thousands of threads of business his spirit never stalled.
translations.idiomatic: When he occupied the chief minister's seat he managed the pivots of state; amid thousands of threads of business his spirit never stalled.

sentences.zh: 自天保五年已後，一人喪德，維持匡救，實有賴焉。

translations.literal: From the fifth year of Tianbao onward, when one man lost virtue, the maintenance and rescue of the realm truly depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: From the fifth year of Tianbao onward, when one man lost virtue, the realm's maintenance and rescue truly depended on him.

sentences.zh: 每天子臨軒，公卿拜授，施號發令，宣揚詔冊，愔辭氣溫辯，神儀秀髮，百寮觀聽，莫不悚動。

translations.literal: Whenever the Son of Heaven faced the throne and the public ministers received appointments, issued orders, and proclaimed edicts, Yin's words were warm and eloquent, his spirit and bearing splendid; the hundred officials who watched and listened were all awestruck.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Son of Heaven faced the throne and ministers received appointments, issued orders, and proclaimed edicts, Yin's words were warm and eloquent and his bearing splendid; the hundred officials who watched were all awestruck.

sentences.zh: 自居大位，門絕私交。

translations.literal: Once he occupied the highest position, his gate was closed to private associations.
translations.idiomatic: Once he occupied the highest position, he shut his gate to private associations.

sentences.zh: 輕貨財，重仁義，前後賞賜，積累巨萬，散之九族；

translations.literal: He lightly regarded wealth and heavily valued benevolence and duty; rewards before and after accumulated to vast sums, which he distributed among the nine clans;
translations.idiomatic: He lightly regarded wealth and heavily valued benevolence and duty; rewards accumulated to vast sums, which he distributed among the nine clans;

sentences.zh: 架篋之中，唯有書數千卷。

translations.literal: In the racks and cases there were only several thousand volumes of books.
translations.idiomatic: in his racks and cases there were only several thousand volumes of books.

sentences.zh: 太保、平原王隆之與愔鄰宅，愔嘗見其門外有富胡數人，謂左右曰：「我門前幸無此物。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian Prince of Pingyuan Longzhi was Yin's neighbor; Yin once saw several rich barbarians outside his gate and said to those beside him, "Fortunately there is nothing like this before my gate."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian Prince of Pingyuan Longzhi was Yin's neighbor; Yin once saw several wealthy barbarians outside his gate and said to those beside him, "Fortunately there is nothing like that before my gate."

sentences.zh: 」性周密畏慎，恆若不足，每聞後命，愀然變色。

translations.literal: His nature was meticulous, cautious, and fearful, always as if insufficient; whenever he heard a later appointment, his expression changed with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was meticulous and cautious, always as if insufficient; whenever he heard a later appointment his expression changed with alarm.

sentences.zh: 文宣大漸，以常山、長廣二王位地親逼，深以後事為念。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan was critically ill, because the two princes of Changshan and Changgung were close in rank and position, he deeply concerned himself with affairs after his death.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan was critically ill, because the princes of Changshan and Changgung were close in rank and position, he was deeply concerned about affairs after his death.

sentences.zh: 愔與尚書左僕射平秦王歸彥、侍中燕子獻、黃門侍郎鄭子默受遺詔輔政，並以二王威望先重，咸有猜忌之心。

translations.literal: Yin, together with Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yan Zixian, and Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate Zheng Zimo, received the deathbed edict to assist in government; because the two princes' prestige had long been weighty, they all harbored suspicions.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, together with left vice director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, attendant-in-ordinary Yan Zixian, and attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate Zheng Zimo, received the deathbed edict to assist in government; because the two princes' prestige had long been weighty, they all harbored suspicions.

sentences.zh: 初在晉陽，以大行在殯，天子諒訚，議令常山王在東館，欲奏之事皆先諮決，二旬而止。

translations.literal: Initially at Jinyang, because the late emperor's coffin was in mourning and the Son of Heaven was in silent grief, it was proposed that the Prince of Changshan stay in the eastern hall, and all matters to be memorialized should first be consulted and decided — for twenty days only.
translations.idiomatic: Initially at Jinyang, because the late emperor's coffin was in mourning and the Son of Heaven was in silent grief, it was proposed that the Prince of Changshan stay in the eastern hall and that all matters to be memorialized should first be consulted and decided — for twenty days only.

sentences.zh: 仍欲以常山王隨梓宮之鄴，留長廣鎮晉陽。

translations.literal: They still wished to have the Prince of Changshan follow the bier to Ye and leave the Prince of Changgung to garrison Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: They still wanted the Prince of Changshan to follow the bier to Ye and the Prince of Changgung to remain and garrison Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 執政復生疑貳，兩王又俱從至於鄴。

translations.literal: The regents again grew doubtful and divided; both princes also followed together to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The regents again grew doubtful and divided; both princes followed together to Ye as well.

sentences.zh: 子獻立計。

translations.literal: Zixian devised a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zixian came up with a plan.

sentences.zh: 欲處太皇太后于北宮，政歸皇太后。

translations.literal: They wished to place the Grand Empress Dowager in the northern palace and return government to the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to place the Grand Empress Dowager in the northern palace and return government to the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 又自天保八年已來，爵賞多濫，至是，愔先自表解其開封王，諸叨竊榮恩者皆從黜免。

translations.literal: Also from the eighth year of Tianbao onward, titles and rewards had been lavishly bestowed; at this time Yin first memorialized requesting to relinquish his title as Prince of Kaifeng, and all who had improperly received honors were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Also from the eighth year of Tianbao onward titles and rewards had been lavishly bestowed; at this time Yin first memorialized requesting to relinquish his title as Prince of Kaifeng, and all who had improperly received honors were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 由是嬖寵失職之徒盡歸心二叔。

translations.literal: Because of this, favorites who lost their posts all turned their hearts to the two uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, favorites who had lost their posts all turned their hearts to the two uncles.

sentences.zh: 高歸彥初雖同德，後尋反動，以疏忌之跡，盡告兩王。

translations.literal: Gao Guiyan had at first shared the same virtue, but later turned rebellious and reported all signs of estrangement and suspicion to the two princes.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Guiyan had at first shared the same purpose, but later turned rebellious and reported all signs of estrangement and suspicion to the two princes.

sentences.zh: 可硃渾天和又每云：「若不誅二王，少主無自安之理。

translations.literal: Kezhuhun Tianhe also repeatedly said, "If the two princes are not executed, the young lord has no means of securing himself."
translations.idiomatic: Kezhuhun Tianhe also repeatedly said, "If the two princes are not executed, the young lord has no way to secure himself."

sentences.zh: 」宋欽道面奏帝，稱二叔威權既重，宜速去之。

translations.literal: Song Qindao memorialized the emperor in person, saying the two uncles' authority and prestige were already heavy and they should be removed quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qindao memorialized the emperor in person, saying the two uncles' authority and prestige were already great and they should be removed quickly.

sentences.zh: 帝不許曰：「可與令公共詳其事。

translations.literal: The emperor would not agree and said, "This may be discussed in detail with the Chief Minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and said, "This may be discussed in detail with the Chief Minister."

sentences.zh: 」愔等議出二王為刺史，以帝仁慈，恐不可所奏，乃通啟皇太后，具述安危。

translations.literal: Yin and the others proposed sending the two princes out as regional inspectors; because the emperor was benevolent, they feared what they memorialized could not be approved, and so they sent a secret report to the Empress Dowager, fully setting forth the danger and safety.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and the others proposed sending the two princes out as regional inspectors; because the emperor was benevolent they feared their memorial would not be approved, and so they sent a secret report to the Empress Dowager fully setting forth the danger.

sentences.zh: 有宮人李昌儀者，北豫州刺史高仲密之妻，坐仲密事入宮。

translations.literal: There was a palace woman Li Changyi, wife of Regional Inspector of Northern Yu Province Gao Zhongmi, who entered the palace because of Zhongmi's case.
translations.idiomatic: There was a palace woman named Li Changyi, wife of Regional Inspector of Northern Yu Gao Zhongmi, who entered the palace because of Zhongmi's case.

sentences.zh: 太后與昌儀宗情，甚相昵愛。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and Changyi were related by clan affection and were very intimate and fond.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager and Changyi were related by clan ties and were very close.

sentences.zh: 太后以啟示之，昌儀密白太皇太后。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager showed her the secret report; Changyi secretly informed the Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager showed her the secret report, and Changyi secretly informed the Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 愔等又議不可令二王俱出，乃奏以長廣王為大司馬、并州刺史，常山王為太師、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Yin and the others also debated that the two princes must not both be sent out, and memorialized making the Prince of Changgung Grand Marshal and Regional Inspector of Bing Province, and the Prince of Changshan Grand Preceptor and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and the others also argued that the two princes must not both be sent away, and memorialized making the Prince of Changgung grand marshal and inspector of Bingzhou, and the Prince of Changshan grand preceptor and supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及二王拜職，於尚書省大會百寮，愔等並將同赴。

translations.literal: When the two princes received their appointments, a great assembly of the hundred officials was held at the Ministry of the Masters of Writing, and Yin and the others were all about to go together.
translations.idiomatic: When the two princes received their appointments, a great assembly of the hundred officials was held at the Ministry of the Masters of Writing, and Yin and the others were all about to attend together.

sentences.zh: 子默止之云：「事不可量，不可輕脫。

translations.literal: Zimo stopped them, saying, "The matter cannot be measured — you must not lightly expose yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Zimo stopped them, saying, "The outcome cannot be foreseen — you must not go lightly."

sentences.zh: 」愔云：「吾等至誠體國，豈有常山拜職，有不赴之理？

translations.literal: Yin said, "We serve the state with utmost sincerity — could there be any reason not to attend when the Prince of Changshan receives his appointment?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "We serve the state with utmost sincerity — how could we fail to attend when the Prince of Changshan receives his appointment?"

sentences.zh: 何為忽有此慮？

translations.literal: Why suddenly have such worries?
translations.idiomatic: Why these sudden worries?

sentences.zh: 」長廣旦伏家僮數十人于錄尚書後室，仍與席上勳貴數人相知，並與諸勳胄約：行酒至愔等，我各勸雙杯，彼必致辭，我一曰「捉酒」，二曰「捉酒」，三曰「何不捉，」爾輩即捉。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changgung had several dozen household slaves lie in wait in the rear chamber behind the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and also made contact with several meritorious nobles at the feast; he agreed with the meritorious scions: when wine reached Yin and the others, each of us will urge a double cup — they will certainly decline — at the first I say 'seize the wine,' at the second 'seize the wine,' at the third 'why not seize?' — then you seize them.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changgung hid several dozen household slaves in the rear chamber behind the supervisor of the Masters of Writing and coordinated with several meritorious nobles at the feast. He agreed with the meritorious scions: when wine reached Yin and the others, each of us will urge a double cup — they will certainly decline — at the first I say 'seize the wine,' at the second 'seize the wine,' at the third 'why not seize?' — then you seize them.

sentences.zh: 及宴如之。

translations.literal: At the feast it happened just so.
translations.idiomatic: At the feast things happened just as he had said.

sentences.zh: 愔大言曰：「諸王反逆，欲殺忠良邪！

translations.literal: Yin cried out loudly, "Princes, you rebel and plot treason — do you wish to kill the loyal and good!"
translations.idiomatic: Yin cried out, "Princes, you rebel and plot treason — do you wish to kill the loyal and good!"

sentences.zh: 尊天子，削諸侯，赤心奉國，未應及此。

translations.literal: Honor the Son of Heaven and reduce the feudal lords — with loyal hearts serving the state, this should not happen.
translations.idiomatic: Honor the Son of Heaven and reduce the feudal lords — with loyal hearts serving the state, this should not come to pass.

sentences.zh: 」常山王欲緩之，長廣王曰：「不可。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changshan wished to ease matters, but the Prince of Changgung said, "It cannot be."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changshan wanted to ease matters, but the Prince of Changgung said, "It cannot be."

sentences.zh: 」於是愔及天和、欽道皆被拳杖亂毆擊，頭面血流，各十人持之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yin, Tianhe, and Qindao were all beaten with fists and clubs in disorder; blood flowed from head and face; ten men each held them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yin, Tianhe, and Qindao were beaten with fists and clubs until blood flowed from head and face; ten men each held them.

sentences.zh: 使薛孤延、康買執子默于尚藥局。

translations.literal: They had Xue Guyian and Kang Mai seize Zimo at the Bureau of Imperial Medicines.
translations.idiomatic: They had Xue Guyian and Kang Mai seize Zimo at the Imperial Medicines Bureau.

sentences.zh: 子默曰：「不用智者言，以至於此，豈非命也！」

translations.literal: Zimo said, "Because I did not heed the words of the wise, it has come to this — is it not fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Zimo said, "Because I did not heed the words of the wise, it has come to this — is this not fate!"

sentences.zh: 二叔率高歸彥、賀拔仁、斛律金擁愔等唐突入雲龍門。

translations.literal: The two uncles led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulü Jin in forcing Yin and the others to burst into the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The two uncles led Gao Guiyan, Heba Ren, and Hulü Jin in forcing Yin and the others to burst through the Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 見都督叱利騷，招之不進，使騎殺之。

translations.literal: They saw Commander Chilì Sao, summoned him but he would not advance, and had horsemen kill him.
translations.idiomatic: They saw Commander Chilì Sao, summoned him but he would not come forward, and had horsemen kill him.

sentences.zh: 開府成休寧拒門，歸彥喻之，乃得入。

translations.literal: Opening General Cheng Xiuning blocked the gate; Guiyan persuaded him, and only then could they enter.
translations.idiomatic: Opening General Cheng Xiuning barred the gate; Guiyan persuaded him, and only then could they enter.

sentences.zh: 送愔等於御前。

translations.literal: They sent Yin and the others before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They brought Yin and the others before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 長廣王及歸彥在硃華門外。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changgung and Guiyan were outside the Vermilion Flower Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changgung and Guiyan waited outside the Vermilion Flower Gate.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后臨昭陽殿，太后及帝側立。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager came to Zhaoyang Hall; the Empress Dowager and the emperor stood to one side.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager came to Zhaoyang Hall; the Empress Dowager and the emperor stood aside.

sentences.zh: 常山王以磚叩頭，進而言曰：「臣與陛下骨肉相連。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changshan knocked his head on a brick and advanced, saying, "Your subject and Your Majesty are joined in flesh and blood.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changshan knocked his head on a brick and stepped forward, saying, "Your subject and Your Majesty are joined in flesh and blood.

sentences.zh: 楊遵彥等欲擅朝權，威福自己，自王公以還，皆重足屏氣，共相脣齒，以成亂階。

translations.literal: Yang Zunyan and the others wished to monopolize court power and make authority and favor their own; from the kings and dukes downward all stood on tiptoe holding their breath, mutually supporting one another like lips and teeth, thereby completing the steps of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunyan and the others wanted to monopolize court power and make authority and favor their own; from the kings and dukes downward all stood on tiptoe holding their breath, mutually supporting one another like lips and teeth, thereby completing the steps of disorder.

sentences.zh: 若不早圖，必為宗社之害。

translations.literal: If we do not plot early, they will surely be a harm to the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not act early, they will surely harm the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 臣與湛等為國事重，賀拔仁、斛律金等惜獻皇帝業，共執遵彥等，領入宮，未敢刑戮。

translations.literal: Your subject and Zhan and the others, because state affairs were weighty, and Heba Ren, Hulü Jin, and the others cherished the enterprise of Emperor Xianwu, together seized Zunyan and the others and led them into the palace, not yet daring to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject and Zhan and the others, because state affairs were weighty, and Heba Ren, Hulü Jin, and the others cherished the enterprise of Emperor Xianwu, together seized Zunyan and the others and led them into the palace, not yet daring to put them to death.

sentences.zh: 專輒之失，罪合萬死。

translations.literal: The offense of acting on one's own authority deserves death ten thousand times over.
translations.idiomatic: The offense of acting on one's own authority deserves death a thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 」帝時默然。

translations.literal: The emperor at that time was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at that moment was silent.

sentences.zh: 領軍劉桃枝之徒陛衛，叩刀仰視，帝不睨之。

translations.literal: The palace guards of Palace Commander Liu Taozhi and the like, with swords drawn, looked up; the emperor would not glance at them.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guards of Palace Commander Liu Taozhi and the like, with swords drawn, looked up; the emperor would not so much as glance at them.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后令卻仗不肯，又厲聲曰：「奴輩即今頭落！

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager ordered them to withdraw their weapons but they refused; she again said fiercely, "Slaves — your heads will fall this instant!"
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager ordered them to sheathe their weapons but they refused; she again said fiercely, "Slaves — your heads will fall this instant!"

sentences.zh: 」乃卻。

translations.literal: Only then did they withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did they fall back.

sentences.zh: 因問楊郎何在，賀拔仁曰：「一目已出。

translations.literal: She then asked where Yang Lang was; Heba Ren said, "One eye is already out."
translations.idiomatic: She then asked where Yang Lang was; Heba Ren said, "One of his eyes is already out."

sentences.zh: 」太皇太后愴然曰：「楊郎何所能，留使不好邪？

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager said sorrowfully, "What could Yang Lang do — was keeping him not better?"
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager said sorrowfully, "What harm could Yang Lang do — was it not better to have kept him?"

sentences.zh: 」乃讓帝曰：「此等懷逆，欲殺我二兒，次及我耳。

translations.literal: She then reproached the emperor, saying, "These men harbored treason and wished to kill my two sons, and next it would reach me.
translations.idiomatic: She then reproached the emperor, saying, "These men harbored treason and wished to kill my two sons, and next it would have reached me.

sentences.zh: 何縱之？

translations.literal: Why spare them?
translations.idiomatic: Why should they be spared?

sentences.zh: 」帝猶不能言。

translations.literal: The emperor still could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still could not find his voice.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后怒且悲，王公皆泣。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager was angry and grieved; the kings and dukes all wept.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager was both angry and grieved; the kings and dukes all wept.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后曰：「豈可使我母子受漢老嫗斟酌。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager said, "How could I let my son and I be arranged at the discretion of an old Han woman."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager said, "How could I let my son and me be arranged at the discretion of an old Han woman."

sentences.zh: 」太后拜謝。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager bowed apologetically.

sentences.zh: 常山王叩頭不止。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changshan kept knocking his head without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changshan kept knocking his head without cease.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后謂帝：「何不安慰爾叔？

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager said to the emperor, "Why do you not comfort your uncle?"
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager said to the emperor, "Why will you not comfort your uncle?"

sentences.zh: 」帝乃曰：「天子亦不敢與叔惜，豈敢惜此漢輩！

translations.literal: The emperor then said, "The Son of Heaven dares not begrudge his uncle — how could he begrudge these Han fellows!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said, "The Son of Heaven dares not begrudge his uncle — how could he begrudge these Han men!"

sentences.zh: 但願乞兒性命，兒自下殿去，此等任叔父處分。

translations.literal: I only beg for my own life — I will descend from the hall myself; these men are yours to dispose of, uncle.
translations.idiomatic: I only beg for my own life — I will leave the hall myself; these men are yours to dispose of, uncle.

sentences.zh: 」遂皆斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Then all were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 長廣王以子默昔讒己，作詔書，故先拔其舌，截其手。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in composing an edict, therefore first pulled out his tongue and cut off his hands.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changgung, because Zimo had once slandered him in composing an edict, first pulled out his tongue and cut off his hands.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后臨愔喪，哭曰：「楊郎忠而獲罪。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager attended Yin's funeral and wept, saying, "Yang Lang was loyal yet suffered guilt."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager attended Yin's funeral and wept, saying, "Yang Lang was loyal yet suffered punishment."

sentences.zh: 」以禦金為之一眼，親內之，曰：「以表我意。

translations.literal: She made an eye of imperial gold for him, placed it inside herself, and said, "To express my intent."
translations.idiomatic: She made an eye of imperial gold for him, placed it inside, and said, "To express my intent."

sentences.zh: 」常山亦悔殺之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changshan also regretted killing him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Changshan also came to regret killing him.

sentences.zh: 先是童謠曰：「白羊頭毣禿，羖腚曆頭生角。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a children's song saying, "White sheep head all bald, ram rump with horn growing on the crown."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been a children's song: "White sheep head all bald, ram rump with horn growing on the crown."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「羊羊吃野草，不吃野草遠我道，不遠打爾腦。

translations.literal: It also said, "Sheep sheep eat wild grass; if you do not eat wild grass stay far from my road — if you do not stay far I will smash your head."
translations.idiomatic: It also ran, "Sheep sheep eat wild grass; if you do not eat wild grass stay far from my road — if you do not stay far I will smash your head."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「阿肼姑，禍也；

translations.literal: It also said, "A-bing-gu, calamity;"
translations.idiomatic: It also said, "A-bing-gu means calamity;"

sentences.zh: 道人姑夫，死也。

translations.literal: Dao-ren gu-fu, death.
translations.idiomatic: Dao-ren gu-fu — death.

sentences.zh: 」羊為愔也，「角」文為用刀，「道人」謂廢帝小名，太原公主嘗作尼，故曰「阿肼姑」，愔、子獻、天和皆尚帝姑，故曰「道人姑夫」云。

translations.literal: Sheep referred to Yin; 'horn' written as a character is 'use knife'; 'Dao-ren' referred to the deposed emperor's childhood name; the Princess of Taiyuan had once become a nun, hence 'A-bing-gu'; Yin, Zixian, and Tianhe all married the emperor's aunts, hence 'Dao-ren gu-fu.'
translations.idiomatic: "Sheep" referred to Yin; the character for "horn" contains "use knife"; "Dao-ren" referred to the deposed emperor's childhood name; the Princess of Taiyuan had once become a nun, hence "A-bing-gu"; Yin, Zixian, and Tianhe all married the emperor's aunts, hence "Dao-ren gu-fu."

sentences.zh: 於是乃以天子之命，下詔罪之；

translations.literal: Thereupon by the Son of Heaven's command an edict was issued condemning them;
translations.idiomatic: Then, by the Son of Heaven's command, an edict was issued condemning them;

sentences.zh: 罪止一身，家口不問。

translations.literal: Guilt was limited to the persons themselves; households were not investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt was limited to the persons themselves; their households were not investigated.

sentences.zh: 尋復簿錄五家，王晞固諫，乃各沒一房，孩幼盡死，兄弟皆除名。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the registers of five families were again copied; Wang Xi firmly remonstrated, and so only one branch of each was confiscated; infants and young were all killed; brothers were all removed from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the registers of five families were again copied; Wang Xi firmly remonstrated, and so only one branch of each was confiscated; infants and young children were all killed; brothers were all removed from the registers.

sentences.zh: 遵彥死，仍以中書令趙彥深代總機務。

translations.literal: After Zunyan's death, Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhao Yanshen was again appointed in his place to oversee the pivots of state.
translations.idiomatic: After Zunyan's death, Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhao Yanshen was again appointed in his stead to oversee the pivots of state.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚少卿陽休之私謂人曰：「將涉千里，殺騏驥而榮蹇驢，可悲之甚！

translations.literal: Supervisor of Guests Yang Xiuzhi privately told someone, "About to travel a thousand leagues, yet killing the fine steed and honoring the lame donkey — how deeply lamentable!"
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of Guests Yang Xiuzhi privately told someone, "About to travel a thousand leagues, yet killing the fine steed and honoring the lame donkey — how lamentable!"

sentences.zh: 」愔所著詩賦表奏書論甚多，誅後散失，門生鳩集所得者萬餘言。

translations.literal: Yin's compositions of poetry, fu, memorials, and treatises were very numerous; after his execution they were scattered and lost, and what his disciples collected amounted to more than ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: Yin wrote a great deal of poetry, fu, memorials, and treatises; after his execution they were scattered and lost, and what his disciples collected amounted to more than ten thousand words.

sentences.zh: 鄭頤字子默，彭城人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi, style name Zimo, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi, styled Zimo, was a man of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖據，魏彭城太守，自滎陽徙焉。

translations.literal: His founding ancestor Ju was Grand Administrator of Pengcheng in Wei and moved from Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His founding ancestor Ju served as Grand Administrator of Pengcheng in Wei and moved from Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 頤聰敏，頗涉文義，而邪險不良。

translations.literal: Yi was clever and quick, somewhat versed in literary principles, but devious and wicked by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was clever and quick, somewhat versed in letters, but devious and wicked by nature.

sentences.zh: 初為太原公東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: At first he was Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 天保世，稍遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he was gradually promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he was gradually promoted to attendant gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與宋欽道特相友愛，欽道每師事之。

translations.literal: He was especially friendly with Song Qindao; Qindao always treated him as a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially friendly with Song Qindao, who always treated him as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 楊愔始輕宋、鄭，不為之禮。

translations.literal: Yang Yin at first looked down on Song and Zheng and did not extend them courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yang Yin looked down on Song and Zheng and did not extend them courtesy.

sentences.zh: 俄而自結人主，稍不可制。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they attached themselves to the ruler and gradually could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they attached themselves to the ruler and gradually grew beyond control.

sentences.zh: 欽道舊與濟南款狎，共相引致，無所不言。

translations.literal: Qindao had long been intimate with Jinan, mutually drawing one another in; there was nothing they did not speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Qindao had long been intimate with Jinan, drawing one another in; there was nothing they did not discuss.

sentences.zh: 乾明初，拜散騎常侍，兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was appointed Regular Cavaliers-in-Attendant and concurrent Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianming he was appointed regular cavaliers-attendant and concurrent attendant gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二人權將楊愔相埒。

translations.literal: The two men's power nearly matched Yang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The two men's power nearly matched Yang Yin's.

sentences.zh: 愔見害之時，邢子才流涕曰：「楊令君雖其人，死日恨不得一佳伴。

translations.literal: When Yin was killed, Xing Zicai wept and said, "Intendant Yang was indeed the man — on the day of his death he regrettably did not have one worthy companion."
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was killed, Xing Zicai wept and said, "Intendant Yang was indeed the man — on the day of his death he sadly lacked one worthy companion."

sentences.zh: 」頤後與愔同詔追贈殿中尚書、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Later Yi, by the same edict as Yin, was posthumously awarded Director of the Palace Department and Regional Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yi, by the same edict as Yin, was posthumously honored as director of the palace department and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 頤弟抗，字子信，頗有文學。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Kang, style name Zixin, was quite accomplished in letters.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Kang, styled Zixin, was quite accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 武平末，兼左右郎中，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: Late in Wuping he was concurrently Left and Right Gentleman and awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuping he was concurrently left and right gentleman and awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 楊敷，字文衍，播族孫也。

translations.literal: Yang Fu, style name Wenyuan, was a clan nephew of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu, styled Wenyuan, was a clan nephew of Bo.

sentences.zh: 高祖暉，洛州刺史，贈恆農公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: His founding ancestor Hui was Regional Inspector of Luo Province and was posthumously awarded Duke of Hengnong with the posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His founding ancestor Hui was regional inspector of Luozhou and was posthumously honored as Duke of Hengnong with the posthumous name Jian (Plain).

sentences.zh: 曾祖恩，河間太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather En was Grand Administrator of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather En was grand administrator of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 祖鈞，博學強識，頗有幹用。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jun was broadly learned with strong memory and possessed considerable practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun was broadly learned with a formidable memory and possessed considerable practical ability.

sentences.zh: 位七兵尚書、北道行台、恆州刺史、懷朔鎮將，贈侍中、司空公，進封臨貞縣伯，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He attained the rank of Minister of the Seven Armies, Northern Route Mobile Headquarters, Regional Inspector of Heng Province, and Garrison Commander of Huaishuo; posthumously he was awarded Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke of Works, advanced in enfeoffment to Baron of Linzhen, with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of the seven armies, Northern Route Mobile Headquarters, regional inspector of Hengzhou, and garrison commander of Huaishuo; posthumously he was honored as attendant-in-ordinary and Duke of Works, advanced in enfeoffment to Baron of Linzhen, with the posthumous name Gong (Respectful).

sentences.zh: 父暄，字宣和。

translations.literal: His father Xuan, style name Xuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan, styled Xuanhe.

sentences.zh: 性通朗，強識有學。

translations.literal: His nature was open and clear, with strong memory and learning.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was open and clear, with a formidable memory and learning.

sentences.zh: 位諫議大夫，以別將從廣陽王深征葛榮，遇害。

translations.literal: He was Remonstrance and Criticism Grandee and as a separate commander followed Prince of Guangyang Shen in campaigning against Ge Rong, and met his end.
translations.idiomatic: He was remonstrance and criticism grandee and as a separate commander followed Prince of Guangyang Shen in campaigning against Ge Rong, and met his end.

sentences.zh: 贈殿中尚書、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded Director of the Palace Department and Regional Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as director of the palace department and regional inspector of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 敷少有志操，重然諾，人景慕之。

translations.literal: Fu from youth had resolve and integrity, valued keeping promises, and people admired and looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu from youth had resolve and integrity, valued keeping promises, and people admired him.

sentences.zh: 魏建義初，襲祖鈞爵臨貞縣伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi in Wei, he inherited his grandfather Jun's barony of Linzhen.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era in Wei, he inherited his grandfather Jun's barony of Linzhen.

sentences.zh: 稍遷廷尉少卿，斷獄以平允稱。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Justice and was known for fair and even judgment of cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to vice director of the Court of Justice and was known for fair and even judgment of cases.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔踐阼，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, his rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, his rank was advanced to marquis, the record states.

sentences.zh: 天和中，為汾州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he was Regional Inspector of Fen Province and his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianhe era he was regional inspector of Fenzhou and his rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 齊將段孝先率眾來寇，城陷見禽。

translations.literal: When Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led troops to invade, the city fell and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi general Duan Xiaoxian led troops to invade, the city fell and he was captured, the record states.

sentences.zh: 齊人方任用之，敷不為屈，遂以憂憤卒於鄴。

translations.literal: The Qi were about to employ him, but Fu would not submit; he therefore died of grief and indignation at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi were about to employ him, but Fu would not submit; he therefore died of grief and indignation at Ye, the record states.

sentences.zh: 子素。

translations.literal: His son Su.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Su.

sentences.zh: 素子處道，少落拓有大志，不拘小節。

translations.literal: Su's son Chudao from youth was unrestrained with great ambition, not bound by minor rules.
translations.idiomatic: Su's son Chudao from youth was unrestrained with great ambition, not bound by minor rules, the record states.

sentences.zh: 世人多未之知，唯從祖寬深異之，每謂子孫曰：「處道逸群絕倫，非常之器，非汝曹所逮。

translations.literal: People of the age mostly did not know him; only his father's younger cousin Kuan deeply regarded him as extraordinary and often told his sons and grandsons, "Chudao surpasses the crowd and stands alone — an instrument out of the ordinary, not something you can reach."
translations.idiomatic: Most people of the age did not know him; only his father's younger cousin Kuan deeply regarded him as extraordinary and often told his sons and grandsons, "Chudao surpasses the crowd and stands alone — an instrument out of the ordinary, not something you can reach."

sentences.zh: 」後與安定牛弘同志好學，研精不倦，多所通涉。

translations.literal: Later he shared the same aspiration with Niu Hong of Anding in loving learning, studying with concentrated effort without weariness, and broadly mastered many fields.
translations.idiomatic: Later he shared the same aspiration with Niu Hong of Anding in loving learning, studying with concentrated effort without weariness, and broadly mastered many fields, the record states.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，工草隸書，頗留意風角。

translations.literal: He was skilled at composing prose, adept at cursive and clerical script, and paid considerable attention to wind omens.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at composing prose, adept at cursive and clerical script, and paid considerable attention to wind omens, the record states.

sentences.zh: 美須髯，有英傑之表。

translations.literal: He had a fine beard and mustache and the bearing of a heroic champion.
translations.idiomatic: He had a fine beard and mustache and the bearing of a heroic champion, the record states.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外記室，轉禮曹，加大都督。

translations.literal: Grand Regent of Zhou Yuwen Hu invited him as Inner and Outer Recording Secretary, transferred him to the Ministry of Rites, and added the rank of Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Regent of Zhou Yuwen Hu invited him as inner and outer recording secretary, transferred him to the Ministry of Rites, and added the rank of grand commander.

sentences.zh: 周武帝親總萬機，素以其父守節陷齊，未蒙朝命，上表申理，至於再三。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou personally took charge of all affairs, Su because his father had kept integrity and fallen into Qi without receiving court appointment, memorialized to state his case, reaching to two and three times.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou personally took charge of all affairs, Su because his father had kept integrity and fallen into Qi without receiving court appointment, memorialized to state his case, reaching to two and three times, the record states.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered those beside him to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered those beside him to behead him, the record states.

sentences.zh: 素又言曰：「臣事無道天子，死其分也。

translations.literal: Su also said, "Your subject serves a ruler without the Way — death is my portion."
translations.idiomatic: Su also said, "I serve a ruler without the Way — death is my portion."

sentences.zh: 」帝悟其言，贈敷使持節、大將軍、譙、廣、復三州刺史，諡曰忠壯。

translations.literal: The emperor took his meaning and posthumously awarded Fu Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General-in-Chief, and Regional Inspector of the three provinces of Qiao, Guang, and Fu, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his meaning and posthumously honored Fu with bearer of the staff of authority, general-in-chief, and inspector of Qiao, Guang, and Fu provinces, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang (Loyal and Stalwart).

sentences.zh: 拜素車騎大將軍、儀同三司，漸見禮遇。

translations.literal: Su was appointed General of the Cavalry and Chariots with Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies and gradually received courtesy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Su was appointed general of the cavalry and chariots with honors equal to the three excellencies and gradually received courtesy and favor.

sentences.zh: 常令為詔，下筆立成，詞義兼美。

translations.literal: He was often ordered to draft edicts; he would set brush to paper and finish at once, with both wording and meaning beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: He was often ordered to draft edicts; he would set brush to paper and finish at once, with both wording and meaning beautiful, the record states.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，謂曰：「善相自勉，勿憂不富貴。

translations.literal: The emperor commended him and said, "Strive to encourage yourself — do not worry about not attaining wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and said, "Encourage yourself — do not worry about failing to attain wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 」素應聲曰：「臣但恐富貴來逼臣，臣無心圖富貴。」

translations.literal: Su answered at once, "Your subject only fears that wealth and rank will press upon him — your subject has no heart to seek wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Su answered at once, "I only fear that wealth and rank will press upon me — I have no heart to seek wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝為丞相，素深自結納，帝甚器之，以為汴州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Su deeply attached himself and won favor; the emperor greatly valued him and made him Regional Inspector of Bian Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Su deeply attached himself and won favor; the emperor greatly valued him and made him regional inspector of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，會尉遲迥作亂。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang, Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Luoyang, Yuchi Jiong rose in rebellion, the record states.

sentences.zh: 滎州刺史宇文胄據武牢應迥，素不得進。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Xing Province Yuwen Zhou held Wulao in response to Jiong, and Su could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector of Xingzhou Yuwen Zhou held Wulao in response to Jiong, and Su could not advance.

sentences.zh: 帝拜素大將軍，擊胄破之。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Su General-in-Chief; he attacked Zhou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Su general-in-chief; he attacked Zhou and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 遷徐州總管，位柱國，封清河郡公，以弟岳為臨貞公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Area Commander of Xu Province, attained the rank of Pillar of State, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe Commandery; his younger brother Yue was made Duke of Linzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to area commander of Xuzhou, attained the rank of pillar of state, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe; his younger brother Yue was made Duke of Linzhen.

sentences.zh: 及隋受禪，加上柱國，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Sui received the abdication, he was given the added rank of Upper Pillar of State and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui received the abdication, he was given the added rank of upper pillar of state and appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 其妻鄭氏性妒悍，素忿之曰：「我若作天子，卿定不堪為皇后。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Zheng was jealous and fierce; Su said in anger, "If I were to become Son of Heaven, you certainly could not bear to be empress."
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Zheng was jealous and fierce; Su said in anger, "If I became Son of Heaven, you certainly could not bear to be empress."

sentences.zh: 」鄭氏奏之，由是坐免。

translations.literal: Lady Zheng reported this, and because of it he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng reported this, and because of it he was dismissed from office, the record states.

sentences.zh: 上方圖江表。

translations.literal: The emperor was then planning for the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then planning for the lands south of the Yangzi, the record states.

sentences.zh: 先是，素數進取陳計。

translations.literal: Earlier Su had repeatedly submitted plans for attacking Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Su had repeatedly submitted plans for attacking Chen, the record states.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜信州總管，賜錢百萬、錦千段、馬二百匹遣之。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Area Commander of Xin Province and was given a million coins, a thousand bolts of brocade, and two hundred horses and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed area commander of Xinzhou and was given a million coins, a thousand bolts of brocade, and two hundred horses and sent off.

sentences.zh: 素居永安，造大艦，名曰五牙，上起樓五層，高百餘尺，左右前後置六檣竿，並高百五十尺，容戰士八百人，旗幟加於上。

translations.literal: Su resided at Yong'an and built a great ship called the Five-Tooth, with a tower of five levels rising more than a hundred feet; on left, right, front, and rear were set six mast poles, each a hundred and fifty feet high, holding eight hundred warriors, with banners and flags added above.
translations.idiomatic: Su resided at Yong'an and built a great ship called the Five-Tooth, with a tower of five levels rising more than a hundred feet; on left, right, front, and rear were set six mast poles, each a hundred and fifty feet high, holding eight hundred warriors, with banners and flags added above, the record states.

sentences.zh: 次曰黃龍，置兵百餘人。

translations.literal: Next came the Yellow Dragon, holding more than a hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Yellow Dragon, holding more than a hundred soldiers, the record states.

sentences.zh: 自余平乘、舴艋等各有差。

translations.literal: The remaining flat-boats, skiffs, and the like each differed in size.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining flat-boats, skiffs, and the like each differed in size, the record states.

sentences.zh: 及大舉攻伐，以素為行軍元帥，引舟師趣三硤。

translations.literal: When the great campaign of attack was launched, Su was made Field Marshal of the campaign and led the fleet toward the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: When the great campaign of attack was launched, Su was made field marshal of the campaign and led the fleet toward the Three Gorges.

sentences.zh: 至流頭灘，陳將戚欣以青龍百餘艘屯兵守狼尾灘，以遏軍路。

translations.literal: When they reached Liutou Shoals, Chen general Qi Xin with more than a hundred Green Dragon ships stationed troops at Langwei Shoals to block the army's route.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Liutou Shoals, Chen general Qi Xin with more than a hundred Green Dragon ships stationed troops at Langwei Shoals to block the army's route, the record states.

sentences.zh: 共地險峭，諸將患之。

translations.literal: The terrain was steep and narrow; the generals were troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain was steep and narrow; the generals were troubled by it, the record states.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「負勝在此一舉，若晝日下船，彼則見我，灘流迅激，制不由人，則吾失其便。

translations.literal: Su said, "Victory depends on this one move. If we disembark by day, they will see us; the shoal currents are swift and violent and cannot be controlled by men — then we lose our advantage."
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Victory hangs on this one move. If we disembark by day, they will see us; the shoal currents are swift and violent and cannot be controlled — then we lose our advantage."

sentences.zh: 」乃夜掩之。

translations.literal: He therefore made a night attack.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore attacked by night.

sentences.zh: 素親率黃龍十艘，銜枚而下。

translations.literal: Su personally led ten Yellow Dragon ships down with rams in the soldiers' mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Su personally led ten Yellow Dragon ships down with rams in the soldiers' mouths, the record states.

sentences.zh: 遣開府王長襲從南岸擊欣別柵。

translations.literal: He sent Opening General Wang Changxi to strike Xin's separate camp from the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Opening General Wang Changxi to strike Xin's separate camp from the south bank, the record states.

sentences.zh: 令大將軍劉仁恩趣白沙北岸。

translations.literal: He ordered Grand General Liu Ren'en to hurry to the north bank of Baisha.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Grand General Liu Ren'en to hurry to the north bank of Baisha, the record states.

sentences.zh: 比明而至，擊之，欣敗。

translations.literal: By dawn they arrived and attacked; Xin was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they arrived and attacked; Xin was defeated.

sentences.zh: 虜其眾，勞而遣之，秋毫不犯，陳人大悅。

translations.literal: They captured his troops, treated them kindly and sent them away, not violating so much as an autumn hair; the people of Chen were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: They captured his troops, treated them kindly and sent them away, not violating so much as an autumn hair; the people of Chen were greatly pleased, the record states.

sentences.zh: 素率水軍東下，舟艦被江，旌甲曜日。

translations.literal: Su led the fleet eastward downriver; the ships covered the river, banners and armor dazzling in the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Su led the fleet eastward downriver; the ships covered the river, banners and armor dazzling in the sun, the record states.

sentences.zh: 素坐平乘大船。

translations.literal: Su sat in a flat-boat great ship.
translations.idiomatic: Su sat aboard a flat-decked great ship.

sentences.zh: 容貌雄偉，陳人望之，懼曰：「清河公即江神也。」

translations.literal: His appearance was heroic and imposing; the people of Chen looked at him and feared, saying, "The Duke of Qinghe is the river god himself."
translations.idiomatic: He looked heroic and imposing; the people of Chen gazed at him in fear, saying, "The Duke of Qinghe is the river god himself."

sentences.zh: 陳南康內史呂仲肅屯岐亭，正據江峽，於北岸纜岩綴鐵鎖三條，橫截上流，以遏戰船。

translations.literal: Chen Interior Secretary of Nankang Lü Zhongsu garrisoned Qiting, directly holding the river gorge; on the north bank he moored iron chains of three strands across the upper stream to block war ships.
translations.idiomatic: Chen interior secretary of Nankang Lü Zhongsu garrisoned Qiting, directly holding the river gorge; on the north bank he moored iron chains of three strands across the upper stream to block war ships.

sentences.zh: 素與仁恩登陸俱發，先攻其柵；

translations.literal: Su and Ren'en went ashore together and launched the attack, first striking his camp;
translations.idiomatic: Su and Ren'en went ashore together and launched the attack, striking his camp first;

sentences.zh: 仲肅軍夜潰，素徐去其鎖。

translations.literal: Zhongsu's army fled by night; Su slowly removed the chains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsu's army fled by night; Su slowly removed the chains, the record states.

sentences.zh: 仲肅復據荊州之延洲。

translations.literal: Zhongsu again held Yanzhou of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsu again held Yanzhou of Jing Province, the record states.

sentences.zh: 素遣巴蜒卒數千，乘五牙四艘，以檣竿碎賊十餘艦，遂大破之，仲肅僅以身免。

translations.literal: Su sent several thousand Ba-Yan soldiers in four Five-Tooth ships; with mast poles they smashed more than ten enemy ships, greatly defeated them, and Zhongsu barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Su sent several thousand Ba-Yan soldiers in four Five-Tooth ships; with mast poles they smashed more than ten enemy ships, greatly defeated them, and Zhongsu barely escaped with his life, the record states.

sentences.zh: 陳主遣其信州刺史顧覺鎮安蜀城，荊州刺史陳紀鎮公安，皆懼而走。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler sent his Regional Inspector of Xin Province Gu Jue to garrison Ancheng and Regional Inspector of Jing Province Chen Ji to garrison Gong'an; both were afraid and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler sent his regional inspector of Xinzhou Gu Jue to garrison Ancheng and regional inspector of Jingzhou Chen Ji to garrison Gong'an; both were afraid and fled.

sentences.zh: 巴陵以東，無敢守者。

translations.literal: East of Baling none dared to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: East of Baling no one dared to hold out.

sentences.zh: 湘州刺史岳陽王陳叔慎請降。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Xiang Province, Prince of Yueyang Chen Shushen requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector of Xiangzhou, Prince of Yueyang Chen Shushen requested surrender.

sentences.zh: 素下至漢口，與秦孝王會，乃還。

translations.literal: Su went down to Hankou and met Prince of Qin Xiaowang, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Su descended to Hankou and met Prince of Qin Xiaowang, then returned.

sentences.zh: 拜荊州總管，進爵郢國公，真食長壽縣千戶；

translations.literal: He was appointed Area Commander of Jing Province, advanced in rank to Duke of Ying State, with a fief of a thousand households in Changshou County;
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed area commander of Jing Province, advanced in rank to Duke of Ying State, with a fief of a thousand households in Changshou County;

sentences.zh: 以其子玄感為儀同三司，玄獎為清河郡公；

translations.literal: His son Xuangan was made Honors Equal to the Three Excellencies and Xuanjiang Duke of Qinghe Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: his son Xuangan was made honors equal to the three excellencies and Xuanjiang Duke of Qinghe;

sentences.zh: 賜物萬段，粟萬石，加之金寶；

translations.literal: He was given ten thousand lengths of goods, ten thousand shi of grain, with gold and jewels added;
translations.idiomatic: he was given ten thousand lengths of goods, ten thousand shi of grain, with gold and jewels added;

sentences.zh: 又賜陳主妹、女妓十四人。

translations.literal: He was also given the Chen ruler's younger sister and fourteen female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: he was also given the Chen ruler's younger sister and fourteen female entertainers.

sentences.zh: 素言於上曰：「裏名勝母，曾子不入，逆人王誼前封郢，臣不願與同。

translations.literal: Su said to the emperor, "Inside a district named Shengmu, Zengzi would not enter; the rebel Wang Yi was once enfeoffed as Duke of Ying — your subject does not wish to share with him."
translations.idiomatic: Su said to the emperor, "In a district named Shengmu, Zengzi would not enter; the rebel Wang Yi was once enfeoffed as Duke of Ying — I do not wish to share a title with him."

sentences.zh: 」於是改封越國公。

translations.literal: Thereupon his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yue State.
translations.idiomatic: Then his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Yue State.

sentences.zh: 尋拜納言，轉內史令。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Chief Counselor and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed chief counselor and transferred to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄而江南人李稜等為亂，以素為行軍總管討之。

translations.literal: Before long Li Ling and others of the Jiangnan region rebelled, and Su was made Field Headquarters Commander to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Ling and others of the Jiangnan region rebelled, and Su was made field headquarters commander to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 帝命平定日，男子悉斬，女婦賞征人，在陣免者從賤。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that on the day of pacification all men were to be beheaded, women given as rewards to the conscript soldiers, and those spared on the battlefield were to be reduced to servile status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that on the day of pacification all men were to be beheaded, women given as rewards to the conscript soldiers, and those spared on the battlefield were to be reduced to servile status, the record states.

sentences.zh: 賊硃莫問自稱南徐州刺史，以盛兵據京口。

translations.literal: The bandit Zhu Mowen styled himself Regional Inspector of Southern Xu and with a strong force held Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Zhu Mowen styled himself regional inspector of Southern Xu and with a strong force held Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 素舟師入自楊子津，進擊破之。

translations.literal: Su's fleet entered from Yangzi Ford and advanced to attack and defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Su's fleet entered from Yangzi Ford and advanced to attack and defeat him, the record states.

sentences.zh: 晉陵顧世興自稱太守，與其都督鮑遷等復來拒戰。

translations.literal: Gu Shixing of Jinling styled himself Grand Administrator and with his Area Commander Bao Qian and others again came to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shixing of Jinling styled himself grand administrator and with his area commander Bao Qian and others again came to resist in battle.

sentences.zh: 素逆擊破之，執遷，虜三千餘人。

translations.literal: Su met and attacked, defeated them, seized Qian, and captured more than three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Su met and attacked, defeated them, seized Qian, and captured more than three thousand men, the record states.

sentences.zh: 進擊無錫賊帥葉皓，又平之。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack the Wuxi bandit chief Ye Hao, he pacified him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to attack the Wuxi bandit chief Ye Hao, he pacified him as well, the record states.

sentences.zh: 吳郡沈玄懀、沈傑等以兵圍蘇州，刺史皇甫績頻戰不利，素率眾援之。
